title.zh: 卷三百八十二 列傳第一百四十一 張燾 黃中 孫道夫 曾幾 勾濤 李彌遜
title.en: Volume 382 Biographies 141: Zhang Dao, Huang Zhong, Sun Daofu, Ceng Ji, Gou Tao, Li Mixun
title.raw: 卷三百八十二 列傳第一百四十一 張燾 黃中 孫道夫 曾幾 勾濤 李彌遜 Volume 382 Biographies 141: Zhang Dao, Huang Zhong, Sun Daofu, Ceng Ji, Gou Tao, Li Mixun

sentences.zh: 張燾，字子公，饒之德興人，秘閣修撰根之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Dao, courtesy name Zigong, was a native of Dexing in Raozhou. He was the son of Gen, a Hanlin academician compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dao, styled Zigong, came from Dexing in Raozhou; he was the son of Gen, who had served as a Hanlin academician compiler.

sentences.zh: 政和八年進士第三人，嘗為辟雍錄、秘書省正字。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenghe he placed third among jinshi degree recipients, and had once served as recorder of the Imperial University and as a proofreader in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked third among jinshi in the eighth year of Zhenghe and had previously held the posts of Imperial University recorder and Secretariat proofreader.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，李綱為親征行營使，辟燾入幕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, when Li Gang was commissioner of the personally-led expeditionary headquarters, he recruited Dao to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang, Li Gang, appointed commissioner of the emperor's field headquarters, brought Dao onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 綱貶，親知坐累者十七人，燾亦貶。

translations.literal: When Gang was demoted, seventeen close associates were implicated and punished; Dao was demoted as well.
translations.idiomatic: After Gang fell from favor, seventeen of his intimates were punished by association, and Dao was demoted too.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，起通判湖州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan reign, he was reappointed and assigned as vice prefect of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era he was recalled to serve as vice prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 明受之變，賊矯詔俾燾撫諭江、浙，燾不受。

translations.literal: During the Mingshou incident, the rebels forged an edict ordering Dao to pacify and reassure the Jiang and Zhe regions, but Dao refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the Mingshou mutiny broke out, the rebels forged an edict commanding Dao to pacify Jiang and Zhe, but he refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 上既復辟，詔求言。

translations.literal: After the emperor had been restored to the throne, an edict was issued soliciting memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had regained the throne, he issued an edict calling for memorials and advice.

sentences.zh: 燾上書略曰：「人主戡定禍亂，未有不本于至誠而能有濟者。

translations.literal: Dao submitted a memorial stating in part: "A ruler who quells calamity and disorder has never succeeded without grounding himself in utmost sincerity."
translations.idiomatic: Dao submitted a memorial that began: "No sovereign has ever put down disaster and rebellion without first rooting his efforts in complete sincerity."

sentences.zh: 陛下踐祚以來，號令之發未足以感人心，政事之施未足以慰人望，豈非在我之誠有未修乎？

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty ascended the throne, the orders you have issued have not been sufficient to move people's hearts, and the policies you have enacted have not been sufficient to satisfy public expectations—is this not because our sincerity has not yet been fully cultivated?
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, your proclamations have failed to stir the people's hearts and your policies have failed to meet their hopes. Is this not because sincerity on our part still falls short?

sentences.zh: 天下治亂，在君子小人用舍而已。

translations.literal: Whether the realm is governed or in disorder depends solely on whether gentlemen or petty men are employed or dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Order and chaos in the empire turn on nothing more than whether the worthy or the base are kept or cast aside.

sentences.zh: 小人之黨日勝，則君子之類日退，將何以弭亂而圖治？

translations.literal: If the faction of petty men grows stronger day by day while the ranks of gentlemen retreat day by day, how will we quell disorder and seek good governance?
translations.idiomatic: As petty men gain ground and gentlemen are pushed back, how can we hope to end turmoil and restore order?

sentences.zh: 」又言措置江防非計，徒費民財、損官賦，不適於用。

translations.literal: He also said that the arrangements for river defenses were ill-conceived, wasting the people's wealth and reducing official revenue without being of practical use.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the river-defense scheme was misguided, squandering public funds and tax revenue while serving no practical purpose.

sentences.zh: 又言：「侍從、臺諫觀望意指，毛舉細務，至國家大事，坐視不言。

translations.literal: He further said: "Attendants and censorial remonstrators watch for the ruler's intent, picking at minor matters, yet on great affairs of state they sit by in silence."
translations.idiomatic: He further wrote: "Court attendants and censorial officials watch for hints of the throne's wishes, nitpicking over trifles, yet on matters vital to the state they remain silent spectators."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「巡幸所至，營繕困民，越棲會稽，似不如是。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Wherever the imperial progress goes, construction and repairs burden the people; when King Goujian of Yue took refuge at Kuaiji, it seems he did not act in this way."
translations.idiomatic: He also observed: "Everywhere the imperial tour passes, building projects exhaust the people—yet when Goujian of Yue made Kuaiji his refuge, he did not behave so."

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，呂頤浩薦，除司勳員外郎，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, on Lü Yihao's recommendation, he was appointed outer-office director in the Ministry of Personnel and promoted to diarist-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shaoxing, recommended by Lü Yihao, he was made outer-office director in the Ministry of Personnel and then promoted to diarist-attendant.

sentences.zh: 言：「自古未有不知敵人之情而能勝者，願詔大臣、諸將，厚爵賞，募可任用者往伺敵動靜。

translations.literal: He said: "From antiquity there has never been one who could prevail without knowing the enemy's situation. I hope Your Majesty will order the chief ministers and generals to offer generous ranks and rewards and recruit capable men to spy on the enemy's movements."
translations.idiomatic: He urged: "No commander in history ever won without understanding the enemy. I ask that ministers and generals be ordered to offer rich rewards and send trustworthy men to observe Jin movements."

sentences.zh: 既審知之，則戰守進退，在我皆備，彼尚安得出不意犯吾行闕。

translations.literal: Once we know this clearly, whether to fight or defend, advance or retreat—all will be in our hands and fully prepared; how then could they take us by surprise and attack our traveling palace?
translations.idiomatic: With clear intelligence in hand, every choice of attack, defense, advance, or retreat would be ours to make; the enemy could hardly hope to strike our mobile court unawares.

sentences.zh: 」詔以付都督府及沿邊諸帥。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that this be transmitted to the grand headquarters and to all frontier commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered his proposal forwarded to the grand headquarters and to every frontier commander.

sentences.zh: 遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the post of Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 呂祉之撫諭淮西也，燾謂張浚曰：「祉書生，不更軍旅，何可輕付。

translations.literal: When Lü Zhi was sent to pacify and reassure Huai West, Dao said to Zhang Jun: "Zhi is a bookish man with no experience in military affairs—how can such a mission be lightly entrusted to him?"
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Zhi was dispatched to pacify Huai West, Dao told Zhang Jun: "Zhi is a scholar who has never served in the army—such a responsibility should not be handed to him so casually."

sentences.zh: 」浚不從，遂致酈瓊之變。

translations.literal: Jun did not heed him, and this led to the uprising of Li Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: Jun refused to listen, and the result was Li Qiong's rebellion.

sentences.zh: 七年，張滉特賜進士出身。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Zhang Huang was specially granted jinshi status.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Zhang Huang was specially awarded jinshi standing.

sentences.zh: 滉，浚兄也，將母至行在，上引對而命之。

translations.literal: Huang was Jun's elder brother; he had brought their mother to the traveling court, and the emperor summoned him for an audience and so ordered it.
translations.idiomatic: Huang was Jun's older brother. He had escorted their mother to the mobile court, and the emperor received him in audience and issued the grant.

sentences.zh: 燾言：「宣和以來，姦臣子弟濫得儒科。

translations.literal: Dao said: "Since the Xuanhe era, the sons and younger brothers of treacherous ministers have indiscriminately obtained civil-service degrees."
translations.idiomatic: Dao protested: "Since Xuanhe, the sons and brothers of corrupt ministers have been showered with civil-service degrees they did not earn."

sentences.zh: 陛下方與浚圖回大業，當以公道革前弊。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is now working with Jun to recover the great enterprise; you ought to reform past abuses through impartial justice.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is now joining Jun in the effort to restore the dynasty; past abuses should be corrected through fair and open standards.

sentences.zh: 今首賜滉第，何以塞公議？

translations.literal: If the first such grant is now given to Huang, how can public criticism be silenced?
translations.idiomatic: If Huang is the first to receive such a favor, how can we answer public outrage?

sentences.zh: 」上念浚功，欲慰其母心，乃命起居郎樓炤行下，炤又封還。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of Jun's merits and wishing to comfort his mother's heart, ordered the diarist-attendant Lou Zhao to promulgate the edict, but Zhao returned it sealed unissued.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, remembering Jun's service and wishing to comfort his mother, ordered diarist-attendant Lou Zhao to issue the edict—but Zhao sealed it and sent it back.

sentences.zh: 著作郎兼起居舍人何掄曰：「賢良之子，宰相之兄，賜科第不為過。

translations.literal: Compilation officer and concurrent diarist-attendant He Lun said: "The son of a worthy man and the elder brother of a chief minister— granting him a degree is not excessive."
translations.idiomatic: He Lun, compilation officer and concurrent diarist-attendant, argued: "He is the son of a virtuous family and the chief minister's own brother—a degree is hardly out of line."

sentences.zh: 」乃與書行。

translations.literal: Thereupon the edict was issued jointly with him.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was then issued with his support.

sentences.zh: 燾不自安，與炤皆求去，不許，言者論之，以集英殿修撰提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: Dao felt ill at ease; both he and Zhao requested dismissal, but this was not granted. Critics memorialized against them, and Dao was made Hanlin academician compiler and superintendent of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dao grew uneasy; he and Zhao both asked to resign, but were refused. Critics attacked them, and Dao was reassigned as Hanlin academician compiler and superintendent of the Taiping Abbey at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，以兵部侍郎召，詔引對，上曰：「卿去止緣張滉。

translations.literal: The following year he was summoned as vice minister of war. An edict ordered an audience, and the emperor said: "Your departure was solely because of Zhang Huang."
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was recalled as vice minister of war. Summoned to audience, the emperor said: "You left office only because of the Zhang Huang affair."

sentences.zh: 」燾曰：「臣苟有所見，不敢不言。

translations.literal: Dao replied: "Whenever your servant has an opinion, he dares not fail to speak."
translations.idiomatic: Dao answered: "Whenever I have a view on a matter, I cannot keep silent."

sentences.zh: 如內侍王鑒，陛下所親信，臣尚論列，豈有宰相親兄自賜出身，公論不與。

translations.literal: Take the eunuch Wang Jian, whom Your Majesty personally trusts—I still memorialized against him. How much less could I remain silent when a chief minister's own brother was granted a degree by special favor, contrary to public opinion?
translations.idiomatic: I spoke out even against the eunuch Wang Jian, whom Your Majesty trusts. How could I say nothing when a chief minister's brother received a degree by special favor that public opinion rejected?

sentences.zh: 臣若不言，豈惟負陛下，亦負張浚。

translations.literal: If your servant had not spoken, would he not have failed not only Your Majesty but Zhang Jun as well?
translations.idiomatic: Had I kept silent, I would have failed not only Your Majesty but Zhang Jun himself.

sentences.zh: 」上因問：「朕圖治一紀，收效蔑然，其弊安在？

translations.literal: The emperor then asked: "I have sought good governance for a full twelve-year cycle, yet results have been negligible—where lies the flaw?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked: "I have pursued good government for twelve years with almost nothing to show for it. Where is the problem?"

sentences.zh: 」燾曰：「自昔有為之君，未有不先定規模而能收效者。

translations.literal: Dao said: "From antiquity, no active ruler has ever achieved results without first setting a fixed plan."
translations.idiomatic: Dao replied: "No effective ruler in history ever achieved results without first establishing a clear strategic plan."

sentences.zh: 臣紹興初首以是為言，今七年。

translations.literal: Your servant first spoke on this point at the beginning of Shaoxing; seven years have now passed.
translations.idiomatic: I raised this very point at the start of Shaoxing—seven years ago.

sentences.zh: 往者進臨大江，退守吳會，未期月而或進或卻，豈不為敵所窺乎？

translations.literal: In the past we advanced to the great river, then retreated to defend Wu and Kuaiji; within less than a month we moved forward or pulled back again— would this not reveal our intentions to the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: We once advanced to the Yangzi, then fell back to Wu and Kuaiji, shifting forward and back within a single month—did the enemy not see through us?

sentences.zh: 今陛下相與斷國論者，二三大臣而已。

translations.literal: Today only two or three chief ministers join Your Majesty in deciding national policy.
translations.idiomatic: Today only two or three senior ministers join Your Majesty in deciding the nation's course.

sentences.zh: 一紀之間，十四命相，執政遞遷無慮二十餘。

translations.literal: Within one twelve-year cycle there have been fourteen appointments of chief ministers, and no fewer than twenty changes among those in executive office.
translations.idiomatic: In twelve years there have been fourteen chief-minister appointments and more than twenty rotations among the top executive ranks.

sentences.zh: 日月逝矣，大計不容復誤，願以先定規模為急。」

translations.literal: The days and months pass; the great plan cannot be mistaken again. I hope Your Majesty will make establishing a fixed plan the urgent priority.
translations.idiomatic: Time is slipping away and the grand strategy cannot be misjudged again. I urge Your Majesty to make setting a firm plan the top priority.

sentences.zh: 尋權吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed acting minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 徽猷閣待制黎確卒，詔贈官推恩，燾言：「確素號正人，一旦臨變，失臣節，北面邦昌之庭，且為將命止勤王之師。

translations.literal: When Hanlin academician Li Que of the Huiyou Pavilion died, an edict ordered posthumous honors and extended favors to his family. Dao said: "Que had long been known as an upright man, yet when crisis came he lost the integrity of a minister, turned north to face Zhang Bangchang's court, and even carried orders to halt the armies coming to rescue the throne."
translations.idiomatic: When Li Que, Hanlin academician of the Huiyou Pavilion, died, the court ordered posthumous honors for him. Dao objected: "Que had been regarded as upright, yet when disaster struck he abandoned ministerial integrity, bowed north toward Zhang Bangchang's court, and even carried orders to stop the armies marching to save the throne."

sentences.zh: 今曲加贈恤，何以示天下？

translations.literal: If extraordinary posthumous honors are now heaped upon him, how will this be shown to the realm?
translations.idiomatic: If we now shower him with special posthumous honors, what message does that send the empire?

sentences.zh: 」詔追奪職名。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that his official titles be posthumously revoked.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered his posthumous titles stripped.

sentences.zh: 時金使至境，詔欲屈己就和，令侍從、臺諫條上。

translations.literal: At that time Jin envoys reached the border. An edict proposed humbling oneself to seek peace and ordered attendants and censorial remonstrators to submit detailed opinions.
translations.idiomatic: Jin envoys had reached the frontier, and an edict proposed bowing to secure peace, ordering court attendants and censorial officials to submit their views in detail.

sentences.zh: 燾言：「金使之來，欲議和好，將歸我梓宮，歸我淵聖，歸我母后，歸我宗社，歸我土地人民，其意甚美，其言甚甘，廟堂以為信然，而群臣、國人未敢以為信然也。

translations.literal: Dao said: "The Jin envoys have come wishing to discuss peace and promising to return our late emperor's coffin, return Emperor Qinzong, return our empress dowager, return our altars of state, and return our lands and people. Their intent sounds very fine and their words very sweet; the court may believe them, but ministers and the people dare not yet believe them."
translations.idiomatic: Dao wrote: "The Jin envoys come speaking of peace—promising the return of our late emperor's remains, of Emperor Qinzong, of the empress dowager, of the altars of state, of our territory and people. Their words sound gracious and their promises sweet. The court may believe them, but ministers and the people do not yet dare to."

sentences.zh: 蓋事關國體，臣請推原天意為陛下陳之。

translations.literal: Since this concerns the integrity of the state, your servant asks leave to trace Heaven's intent and lay it before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Because the nation's honor is at stake, I ask to trace Heaven's intent and lay it before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：『天將興之，誰能廢之？

translations.literal: The Commentary says: 'When Heaven is about to raise someone up, who can cast him down?'
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: 'When Heaven intends to raise a man up, who can cast him down?'

sentences.zh: 』臣考人事以驗天意，陛下飛龍濟州，天所命也。

translations.literal: Your servant examines human affairs to verify Heaven's intent: when Your Majesty ascended like a flying dragon at Jizhou, that was Heaven's command.
translations.idiomatic: I weigh human events to read Heaven's will: when Your Majesty rose like a dragon at Jizhou, that was Heaven's decree.

sentences.zh: 敵騎屢犯行闕，不能為虞。

translations.literal: Enemy horsemen repeatedly assaulted the traveling palace yet could do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Jin cavalry repeatedly struck at the mobile court yet could not touch Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 甲寅一戰敗敵師，丙辰再戰卻劉豫，丁巳酈瓊雖叛，實為偽齊廢滅之資，皆天所贊也。

translations.literal: In jiayin we defeated the enemy army in one battle; in bingchen we repelled Liu Yu in a second; in dingsi, though Li Qiong rebelled, this in fact supplied the means for the abolition of the puppet Qi—all were Heaven's support.
translations.idiomatic: In jiayin we routed the enemy in a single battle; in bingchen we drove back Liu Yu; in dingsi Li Qiong rebelled, yet that rebellion became the very means by which the puppet Qi was destroyed—all of this was Heaven's aid.

sentences.zh: 是蓋陛下躬履艱難，側身修行，布德立正，上副天意，而天佑之之所致也。

translations.literal: This is because Your Majesty personally endured hardship, restrained yourself in conduct, spread virtue and established righteousness, matching Heaven's intent—and Heaven therefore blessed you.
translations.idiomatic: This came about because Your Majesty personally endured hardship, disciplined your conduct, spread virtue, and upheld righteousness in accord with Heaven—and Heaven rewarded you accordingly.

sentences.zh: 臣以是知上天悔禍有期，中興不遠矣。

translations.literal: From this your servant knows that Heaven's repentance of calamity has its appointed time and that restoration is not far off.
translations.idiomatic: From this I know that Heaven's reversal of our disaster has its appointed hour and that restoration is near.

sentences.zh: 願益自修自強，以享天心，以俟天時。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will further cultivate and strengthen yourself, enjoy Heaven's favor, and await Heaven's appointed moment.
translations.idiomatic: I urge Your Majesty to cultivate yourself further, align with Heaven's favor, and wait for the moment Heaven appoints.

sentences.zh: 時之既至，吉無不利，則何戰不勝，何功不立。

translations.literal: When the time arrives, good fortune will attend every undertaking—what battle would not be won, what achievement would not be established?
translations.idiomatic: When the hour comes, fortune will favor every endeavor—what battle could we lose, what achievement could we fail to win?

sentences.zh: 今此和議，姑為聽之，而必無信之可恃也。

translations.literal: As for this peace negotiation for now, let us listen to it, but we must not rely on it as trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: For now we may hear out this peace talk, but we must not treat it as something we can trust.

sentences.zh: 彼使已及境，勢難固拒。

translations.literal: Their envoys have already reached the border; given the situation it would be hard to refuse them outright.
translations.idiomatic: Their envoys are already at the frontier, and circumstances make a flat refusal difficult.

sentences.zh: 使其果願和好，如前所陳，是天誘其衷，必不復強我以難行之禮。

translations.literal: If they truly wish for peace as previously stated, Heaven has moved their hearts and they will not again force upon us rites difficult to perform.
translations.idiomatic: If they genuinely seek peace as they claim, Heaven has moved their hearts and they will not again impose rites we cannot honorably perform.

sentences.zh: 如其初無此心，二三其說，責我以必不可行之禮，要我以必不可從之事，其包藏何所不有，便當以大義絕之。

translations.literal: If from the first they had no such intent, shifting their words this way and that, demanding rites we absolutely cannot perform and requiring things we absolutely cannot accept—what treachery might they not conceal?—then we should break with them on grounds of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: If they never meant peace, shifting their story and demanding rites we cannot perform or concessions we cannot grant—what deception might they not hide?—then we should break with them on principle.

sentences.zh: 謹邊防，厲將士，相時而動。

translations.literal: Guard the frontiers carefully, steel the generals and soldiers, and act according to the opportune moment.
translations.idiomatic: Strengthen the frontiers, harden the troops, and move when the moment is right.

sentences.zh: 願斷自淵衷，毋取必於彼而取必於天而已。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will decide from the depths of your heart to seek certainty not from them but from Heaven alone.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to decide from your inmost heart to rely not on them but on Heaven alone.

sentences.zh: 乃若略國家之大恥，置宗社之深仇，躬率臣民，屈膝于金而臣事之，而凱和議之必成，非臣所敢知也。

translations.literal: As for setting aside the great shame of the state, ignoring the deep enmity against our altars of soil and grain, personally leading ministers and people to kneel before Jin and serve them as subjects, and rejoicing that peace talks will surely succeed—that is not something your servant dares to understand.
translations.idiomatic: As for brushing aside the nation's deepest humiliation, forgetting the gravest injury to our altars of state, leading ministers and people to kneel before Jin and serve as their subjects, and counting on peace as a certainty—that I cannot accept.

sentences.zh: 」上覽奏，愀然變色曰：「卿言可謂忠，然朕必不至為彼所紿，方且熟議，必非詐偽而後可從，不然，當再使審虛實，拘其使人。

translations.literal: When the emperor read the memorial, his expression changed and he said with distress: "Your words are truly loyal, yet I will certainly not be deceived by them. We are deliberating carefully and will agree only if there is no fraud; otherwise we shall send envoys again to verify the truth and detain their ambassadors."
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial, the emperor's face darkened. "Your words are loyal," he said, "but I will not be fooled by Jin. We are deliberating carefully and will agree only if there is no deception; otherwise we will send envoys to verify the facts and detain their ambassadors."

sentences.zh: 」燾頓首謝。

translations.literal: Dao bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Dao kowtowed in acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 金使張通古、蕭哲至行在，朝議欲上拜金詔。

translations.literal: When the Jin envoys Zhang Tonggu and Xiao Zhe reached the traveling court, court discussion favored having the emperor ascend to perform the ritual of bowing to the Jin edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin envoys Zhang Tonggu and Xiao Zhe arrived at the mobile court, court opinion favored having the emperor perform the ritual of bowing to the Jin edict.

sentences.zh: 燾曰：「陛下信王倫之虛詐，發自聖斷，不復謀議，便欲行禮，群臣震懼罔措。

translations.literal: Dao said: "Your Majesty trusts Wang Lun's empty deceit, deciding from your own sacred judgment without further consultation, and now wishes to perform the rite—the ministers are shaken with fear and at a loss."
translations.idiomatic: Dao protested: "Your Majesty trusts Wang Lun's hollow promises, has decided on your own without further deliberation, and now intends to perform the rite—the court is shaken and helpless."

sentences.zh: 必已得梓宮，已得母后，已得宗族，始可議通好經久之禮。

translations.literal: Only after the late emperor's coffin has been recovered, the empress dowager recovered, and the imperial clan recovered may we discuss rites for lasting peace.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the late emperor's remains, the empress dowager, and the imperial clan have all been returned can we discuss rites for lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 今彼特以通好為說，意謂割地講和而已，陛下之所願欲而切於聖心者，無一言及之，其情可見，奈何遽欲屈而聽之。

translations.literal: Now they speak only of establishing friendly relations, meaning merely ceding territory to make peace. What Your Majesty most deeply desires and holds closest to your sacred heart—they mention not a word of it. Their intent is plain—why then rush to bow and heed them?
translations.idiomatic: They speak only of friendship, meaning nothing more than ceding land for peace. Not one word touches what Your Majesty most deeply desires. Their intent is obvious—why rush to submit?

sentences.zh: 一屈之後，不可復伸，廷臣莫能正救，曾魯仲連之不如，豈不獲罪于天下萬世。」

translations.literal: Once we bow once, we cannot straighten again. No court minister can set things right—we are not even the equal of Lu Zhonglian of Zeng. Will we not incur guilt before all the world for ten thousand generations?
translations.idiomatic: Once we bow, we can never stand straight again. No minister can set this right—we fall short even of Lu Zhonglian. Will we not be condemned by all posterity?

sentences.zh: 既而監察御史施廷臣抗章力贊和議，擢為侍御史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward investigating censor Shi Tingchen submitted a forceful memorial in support of the peace talks and was promoted to attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, investigating censor Shi Tingchen submitted a bold memorial endorsing peace and was promoted to attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 司農寺丞莫將忽賜第，擢為起居郎。

translations.literal: Mo Jiang, assistant director in the Directorate of Agriculture, was suddenly granted a residence and promoted to diarist-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Jiang, an assistant director in the Directorate of Agriculture, was suddenly granted an official residence and promoted to diarist-attendant.

sentences.zh: 朝論大駭。

translations.literal: Court opinion was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The court was stunned.

sentences.zh: 燾率吏部侍郎晏敦復上疏曰：

translations.literal: Dao, together with Vice Minister of Personnel Yan Dunfu, submitted a memorial stating:
translations.idiomatic: Dao joined Vice Minister of Personnel Yan Dunfu in submitting a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「仰惟陛下痛梓宮未還，兩宮未復，不憚屈己與敵議和，特以眾論未同，故未敢輕屈爾。

translations.literal: "Looking up, we consider that Your Majesty grieves that the late emperor's coffin has not returned and the two palaces have not been restored, and does not shrink from humbling yourself to negotiate peace with the enemy—only because public opinion is not united have you not yet dared to bow lightly."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty grieves that the late emperor's remains and the two palaces have not been restored, and is willing to humble yourself to negotiate with the enemy—yet because public opinion is not united, you have not yet dared to submit lightly."

sentences.zh: 幸小大之臣，無復異議，從容獻納，庶幾天聽為回，卒不敢屈，此宗社之福也。

translations.literal: Fortunately ministers great and small no longer differ in opinion and can calmly offer advice; perhaps Heaven's ear may be moved and in the end you will not bow—this would be the fortune of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately ministers of every rank now speak with one voice, offering counsel calmly; perhaps Heaven will hear and you will never need to bow—this would be the dynasty's blessing.

sentences.zh: 彼施廷臣乃務迎合，輒敢抗章，力贊此議，姑為一身進用之資，不恤君父屈辱之恥，罪不容誅，乃由察官超擢柱史。

translations.literal: Yet Shi Tingchen seeks only to curry favor, daring to submit a forceful memorial vigorously endorsing this proposal merely as capital for his own advancement, heedless of the shame of his sovereign and father's humiliation—a crime deserving death—yet he is leapfrogged from investigating censor to chief censor.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shi Tingchen seeks only to flatter, daring to submit a forceful memorial endorsing this plan merely to advance himself, heedless of the humiliation of his sovereign—a crime deserving death—yet he is leapfrogged from investigating censor to chief censor.

sentences.zh: 夫御史府，朝廷紀綱之地，而陛下耳目之司，前日勾龍如淵以附會而得中丞，眾論固已喧鄙之矣。

translations.literal: The Censorate is the place where the court's discipline is maintained and Your Majesty's eyes and ears—previously Gou Long Ruyuan obtained the vice censor-in-chief's post through sycophantic compliance, and public opinion had already clamored in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate upholds the court's discipline and serves as Your Majesty's eyes and ears. Gou Long Ruyuan already won the vice censor-in-chief's post through sycophancy, and public opinion already despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 今廷臣又以此而躋橫榻，一臺之中，長貳皆然，既同鄉曲，又同心腹，惟相朋附，變亂是非，豈不紊紀綱而蔽陛下之耳目乎？

translations.literal: Now Tingchen too has risen to the chief censor's seat for this reason. Within one bureau both the chief and deputy are such men—fellow townsmen and confidants alike, banding together in faction and confounding right and wrong. Will this not disorder discipline and blind Your Majesty's eyes and ears?
translations.idiomatic: Now Tingchen too has risen to chief censor for the same reason. Within one bureau both the chief and deputy are alike—townsmen and confidants who band together in faction and confound right and wrong. Will this not destroy discipline and blind Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 眾論沸騰，方且切齒，而莫將者又以此議由寺丞擢右史。

translations.literal: Public opinion seethes and grinds its teeth, yet Mo Jiang too is promoted from assistant director to right diarist-attendant for this same proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Public outrage is boiling, yet Mo Jiang too is promoted from assistant director to right diarist-attendant for endorsing the same plan.

sentences.zh: 如淵、廷臣庸人也，初無所長，但知觀望，而將則姦人也，考其平昔無所不為，此輩烏可與之斷國論乎？

translations.literal: Ruyuan and Tingchen are mediocre men with no special talent who know only how to watch for the prevailing wind, while Jiang is a wicked man whose past conduct shows he stops at nothing. How can such people be allowed to decide national policy?
translations.idiomatic: Ruyuan and Tingchen are mediocrities who know only how to read the wind; Jiang is a villain whose past shows he stops at nothing. How can such men decide the fate of the nation?

sentences.zh: 望加斥逐，庶幾少杜群枉之門。

translations.literal: We hope they will be expelled and driven away, so that the door to factional wrongdoing may be somewhat closed.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that they be expelled, so that the door to corrupt faction may be partly shut.

sentences.zh: 至於和議，則王倫實為謀主，彼往來敵中至再四矣，陛下恃以為心腹，信之如蓍龜，今其為言自己二三事之端倪，蓋亦可見。

translations.literal: As for the peace talks, Wang Lun is in fact the chief plotter. He has traveled back and forth to the enemy's territory three or four times already. Your Majesty treats him as a trusted confidant and believes him as one would trust divination by yarrow or tortoise shell. The signs in two or three things he now says are already visible.
translations.idiomatic: As for peace, Wang Lun is the chief architect. He has shuttled to the enemy three or four times already, and Your Majesty trusts him as one trusts divination. The signs in what he says now are already plain.

sentences.zh: 更望仰念祖宗付託之重，俯念億兆愛戴之誠，貴重此身，無輕于屈。

translations.literal: We further hope Your Majesty will look up and reflect on the heavy trust the ancestors have placed in you, look down and reflect on the sincere devotion of the hundred million people, and hold your person precious—not bow lightly.
translations.idiomatic: We further ask Your Majesty to remember the weight of the ancestors' trust and the devotion of the people, and to hold yourself precious—not to bow lightly.

sentences.zh: 但務雪恥以思復仇，加禮其使，厚資遣發，諭以必得事實之意，告以國人皆曰不可之狀。

translations.literal: Devote yourself only to wiping away shame and planning revenge. Treat their envoys with courtesy, provide them generously for their departure, explain that you must have the facts, and tell them how the people all say it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Devote yourself to wiping away shame and planning revenge. Treat their envoys courteously, provide them generously for their return, insist on verified facts, and tell them the people unanimously reject submission.

sentences.zh: 使彼悔禍，果出誠心，惟我所欲，盡歸於我，然後徐議報之之禮，亦未晚也。

translations.literal: If they repent of calamity and truly show sincere intent, giving back everything we desire and restoring all to us, then to discuss slowly the rites of reciprocation would not yet be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If they repent and show genuine intent, returning everything we demand, then discussing reciprocal rites would not be too late.

sentences.zh: 如其變詐，誘我以虛詞，則包藏終不可測，便當厲將士，保疆塲，自治自強，以俟天時，何為不成？

translations.literal: If they shift in deceit and lure us with empty words, then their hidden designs can never be fathomed—we should steel the generals and soldiers, defend the borders, govern and strengthen ourselves, and await Heaven's appointed time. What could not be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: If they turn deceitful and lure us with empty promises, their hidden designs can never be known—we should harden the troops, defend the borders, strengthen ourselves, and await Heaven's hour. What could we not achieve?

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下少忍而已。

translations.literal: We humbly hope Your Majesty will bear with this a little longer.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly ask Your Majesty to hold firm a little longer.

sentences.zh: 自朝廷有屈己之議，上下解體，儻遂成屈己之事，則上下必至離心，人心既離，何以立國？

translations.literal: Since the court began discussing humbling ourselves, superiors and subordinates have lost cohesion. If we actually carry out self-abasement, superiors and subordinates will inevitably lose heart. Once hearts are divided, how can a state stand?
translations.idiomatic: Since the court began debating submission, the realm has lost cohesion. If submission actually occurs, ruler and people will inevitably part ways. Once hearts are divided, how can the state endure?

sentences.zh: 伏願戒之重之。」

translations.literal: We humbly hope Your Majesty will guard against this and treat it with utmost seriousness."
translations.idiomatic: We humbly urge Your Majesty to guard against this with the utmost seriousness."

sentences.zh: 於是將、廷臣皆不敢拜。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jiang and Tingchen both dared not perform the bowing rite.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon neither Jiang nor Tingchen dared perform the bowing rite.

sentences.zh: 燾又面折如淵曰：「達觀其所舉，君薦七人，皆北面張邦昌，今囁嚅附會，墮敵計，他日必背君親矣。」

translations.literal: Dao also confronted Ruyuan face to face, saying: "I have observed your recommendations. You recommended seven men, all of whom turned north to face Zhang Bangchang. Now you mutter sycophantic compliance and fall into the enemy's scheme—you will betray sovereign and kin one day."
translations.idiomatic: Dao also confronted Ruyuan directly: "I have watched your recommendations. You promoted seven men who all bowed north to Zhang Bangchang. Now you mutter sycophantic compliance and fall into the enemy's trap—you will betray your sovereign and kin one day."

sentences.zh: 燾既力詆拜詔之議，秦檜患之，燾亦自知得罪，託疾在告。

translations.literal: Since Dao had vigorously denounced the proposal to bow to the edict, Qin Hui resented him. Dao also knew he had offended and pleaded illness to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: Because Dao had fiercely opposed bowing to the Jin edict, Qin Hui resented him. Dao knew he had given offense and pleaded illness to stay home.

sentences.zh: 檜使樓炤諭之曰：「北扉闕人，欲以公為直院。

translations.literal: Hui sent Lou Zhao to inform him: "The Northern Secretariat lacks personnel; we wish to appoint you as drafter of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent Lou Zhao to tell him: "The Northern Secretariat needs staff—we wish to appoint you as a drafter."

sentences.zh: 」燾大駭曰：「果有此言，愈不敢出矣。

translations.literal: Dao was greatly alarmed and said: "If such words are truly spoken, I am all the more afraid to emerge."
translations.idiomatic: Dao was deeply alarmed: "If that is truly the offer, I am all the more afraid to leave my house."

sentences.zh: 」檜不能奪，乃止。

translations.literal: Hui could not prevail over him and let the matter drop.
translations.idiomatic: Hui could not change his mind and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 和議成，范如圭請遣使朝八陵，遂命判大宗正士㒟與燾偕行，且命修奉，令荊湖帥臣岳飛濟其役。

translations.literal: When peace was concluded, Fan Rugui requested that envoys be sent to pay court at the eight imperial tombs. The emperor then ordered Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Affairs Bureau Shi Yi to travel together with Dao, and also ordered restoration and maintenance, directing the Jing-Hu commander Yue Fei to supply the labor.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was concluded, Fan Rugui asked that envoys be sent to visit the eight imperial tombs. The emperor ordered Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Bureau Shi Yi to travel with Dao and commanded restoration work, directing Jing-Hu commander Yue Fei to supply the labor.

sentences.zh: 燾與士㒟道武昌，出蔡、潁，河南百姓歡迎夾道，以喜以泣曰：「久隔王化，不圖今日復為宋民。

translations.literal: Dao and Shi Yi traveled by way of Wuchang, passing through Cai and Ying. The people of Henan lined the roads to welcome them, weeping and rejoicing as they said: "Long separated from the king's transforming influence—we never imagined we would today again become subjects of Song."
translations.idiomatic: Dao and Shi Yi traveled via Wuchang through Cai and Ying. Henan people lined the roads to welcome them, weeping and rejoicing: "Long cut off from imperial rule—we never dreamed we would again be subjects of Song."

sentences.zh: 」九年五月，至永安諸陵，朝謁如禮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the ninth year they reached the tombs at Yong'an and paid court according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the ninth year they reached the Yong'an tombs and performed the rites of homage.

sentences.zh: 陵前石澗水久涸，二使垂至忽湧溢，父老驚歎，以為中興之兆。

translations.literal: The stone brook before the tombs had long been dry, but just as the two envoys were about to arrive it suddenly surged and overflowed. The elders marveled, taking it as an omen of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: The stone brook before the tombs had long run dry, but just as the two envoys were about to arrive it suddenly surged. The elders marveled, taking it as an omen of restoration.

sentences.zh: 燾等入柏城，披鉏荊棘，隨所葺治，留二日而還，自鄭州歷汴、宋、宿、泗、淮南以歸。

translations.literal: Dao and the others entered the cypress grove of the tombs, clearing away brambles and thorns with hoes and repairing wherever needed. They stayed two days and returned, traveling from Zhengzhou through Bian, Song, Su, Si, and Huainan on their way home.
translations.idiomatic: Dao and his party entered the tomb grove, hacking through brambles and repairing what they could. After two days they headed back, traveling from Zhengzhou through Bian, Song, Su, Si, and Huainan.

sentences.zh: 即奏疏曰：「金人之禍，上及山陵，雖殄滅之，未足以雪此恥、復此仇也。

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a memorial stating: "The calamity wrought by the Jin reached even to the imperial tombs. Even if we exterminate them, it would not suffice to wipe away this shame or avenge this enmity."
translations.idiomatic: He immediately memorialized: "The Jin disaster reached even the imperial tombs. Exterminating them would not suffice to wipe away this shame or settle this score."

sentences.zh: 陛下聖孝天至，豈勝痛憤，顧以梓宮、兩宮之故，方且與和，未可遽言兵也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's sacred filial piety reaches to Heaven—how could you not be overwhelmed with grief and rage? Yet for the sake of the late emperor's coffin and the two palaces, you are now negotiating peace and cannot yet speak hastily of war.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's filial devotion is heaven-reaching—who could not share your grief and rage? Yet for the sake of the late emperor's remains and the two palaces, you are negotiating peace and cannot yet speak of war.

sentences.zh: 祖宗在天之靈，震怒既久，豈容但已，異時恭行天罰，得無望于陛下乎？

translations.literal: The spirits of the ancestors in Heaven have long been stirred to wrath—how could this simply end? When the time comes to reverently execute Heaven's punishment, will they not look to Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral spirits in Heaven have long burned with wrath—how can this simply end? When Heaven's punishment is carried out, will they not look to Your Majesty?

sentences.zh: 自古戡定禍亂，非武不可，狼子野心不可保恃久矣；

translations.literal: From antiquity, quelling calamity and disorder has never been possible without force. The wolf's cub nature and wild ambition cannot be relied upon for long;
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, putting down disaster and rebellion has always required force. The wolf's cub nature cannot be trusted for long;

sentences.zh: 伏望修武備，俟釁隙起而應之，電掃風驅，盡俘醜類以告諸陵。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will strengthen military preparations, wait until a breach opens and respond, sweeping like lightning and driving like wind, capturing all the enemy host to report to the tombs.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly urge Your Majesty to strengthen the military, wait for an opening, then strike like lightning and report the capture of every enemy to the tombs.

sentences.zh: 夫如是然後盡天子之孝，而為人子孫之責塞矣。

translations.literal: Only thus can the filial piety of a Son of Heaven be fully fulfilled and the duty of a descendant discharged.
translations.idiomatic: Only then can a Son of Heaven fulfill his filial duty and a descendant discharge his obligation.

sentences.zh: 」上問諸陵寢如何，燾不對，唯言：「萬世不可忘此賊。

translations.literal: The emperor asked how the tombs and chambers fared. Dao did not answer directly, saying only: "For ten thousand generations we must not forget this enemy."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked about the condition of the tombs. Dao did not answer directly, saying only: "For ten thousand generations we must not forget this enemy."

sentences.zh: 」上黯然。

translations.literal: The emperor's expression darkened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face fell.

sentences.zh: 燾因請永固陵不用金玉，大略謂：「金玉珍寶，聚而藏之，固足以動人耳目，又其為物，自當流布於世，理必發露，無足怪者。

translations.literal: Dao therefore requested that the Yonggu Tombs not use gold and jade, stating in general: "Gold, jade, and precious treasures gathered and stored away are indeed enough to stir people's eyes and ears. Moreover, as objects they are bound by nature to circulate in the world—inevitably they will be exposed, and there is nothing strange in this."
translations.idiomatic: Dao therefore asked that the Yonggu Tombs use no gold or jade, arguing in essence: "Gold and precious treasures hoarded in tombs are bound to tempt thieves. Such things are meant to circulate in the world—they will inevitably be found, and that is no surprise."

sentences.zh: 」上覽疏，謂秦檜曰：「前世厚葬之禍，如循一軌。

translations.literal: When the emperor read the memorial, he said to Qin Hui: "The calamities of lavish burial in past ages follow a single track."
translations.idiomatic: Reading the memorial, the emperor told Qin Hui: "The disasters of lavish burial in past ages all follow the same pattern."

sentences.zh: 朕斷不用金玉，庶先帝神靈有萬世之安。

translations.literal: I am resolved not to use gold and jade, so that the spirit of the late emperor may have peace for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: I am resolved to use no gold or jade, so that the late emperor's spirit may rest in peace for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 」燾又言：「頃劉豫初廢，人情恟恟，我斥候不明，坐失機會。

translations.literal: Dao further said: "When Liu Yu was recently abolished, public sentiment was in turmoil, yet our scouts were unclear and we sat by and lost the opportunity."
translations.idiomatic: Dao added: "When Liu Yu was recently abolished, the people were in turmoil, yet our intelligence was poor and we missed the opportunity."

sentences.zh: 今又聞敵于淮陽作筏、造繩索，不知安用？

translations.literal: Now we again hear that the enemy at Huaiyang is building rafts and making ropes— for what purpose?
translations.idiomatic: Now we hear the enemy at Huaiyang is building rafts and making ropes—what are they for?

sentences.zh: 諸將朝廷戒勿得遣間探，遂不復遣，我之動息，敵無不知，敵之情狀，我則不聞。

translations.literal: The court has warned the generals not to send spies, so they send none anymore. Our movements the enemy knows all; the enemy's situation we hear nothing of.
translations.idiomatic: The court has forbidden generals to send spies, so none are sent. The enemy knows all our movements; we know nothing of theirs.

sentences.zh: 又見黃河船盡拘北岸，悉為敵用，往來自若，無一人敢北渡者。

translations.literal: We also see that all boats on the Yellow River are detained on the north bank and entirely used by the enemy, who come and go freely, while not a single person dares cross north.
translations.idiomatic: We also see all Yellow River boats detained on the north bank for enemy use—they come and go freely while no one dares cross north.

sentences.zh: 願飭邊吏廣耳目，先事而防。

translations.literal: I hope frontier officials will be ordered to broaden their intelligence and guard against events before they occur.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that frontier officials be ordered to broaden intelligence and prepare before trouble strikes.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「酈瓊部伍皆西陲勁兵，今在河南，尚可收用。

translations.literal: He also said: "Li Qiong's troops are all crack soldiers from the western frontier. Now that they are in Henan, they can still be brought into service."
translations.idiomatic: He also noted: "Li Qiong's troops are crack soldiers from the western frontier. Now in Henan, they could still be put to use."

sentences.zh: 新疆租賦已蠲，而使命絡繹，推恩費用猶循兵興時例，願加裁損，非甚不得已勿遣使，以寬民力。

translations.literal: The newly recovered territories' taxes and levies have already been remitted, yet envoys come in an unbroken stream and the costs of extending favors still follow wartime precedent. I hope these will be cut back and that envoys will not be dispatched except when absolutely necessary, to ease the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes in the newly recovered territories have been remitted, yet envoys stream back and forth and favor-granting costs still follow wartime levels. I urge cutbacks and that envoys be sent only when absolutely necessary, to ease the people's burden.

sentences.zh: 」又論：「陝西諸帥不相下，動輒喧爭，請置一大帥統之，庶首尾相應，緩急可恃。

translations.literal: He also argued: "The commanders in Shaanxi do not defer to one another and constantly quarrel loudly. I ask that one supreme commander be appointed to unify them, so that head and tail may respond together and we may rely on them in urgency."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "The Shaanxi commanders refuse to defer to one another and constantly quarrel. Appoint one supreme commander so they can coordinate and be relied upon in crisis."

sentences.zh: 」燾所言皆切中時病，秦檜方主和，惟恐少忤敵意，悉置不問。

translations.literal: Everything Dao said struck at the ailments of the age, but Qin Hui was then advocating peace and feared giving the slightest offense to the enemy, so he set it all aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Everything Dao said hit the mark, but Qin Hui was pushing peace and feared offending the enemy, so he ignored it all.

sentences.zh: 成都謀帥，上諭檜曰：「張燾可，第道遠，恐其憚行。

translations.literal: When a commander for Chengdu was being sought, the emperor told Hui: "Zhang Dao would do, but the distance is great—I fear he may dread the journey."
translations.idiomatic: When a Chengdu commander was needed, the emperor told Hui: "Zhang Dao would do, but the distance is great—I fear he may hesitate to go."

sentences.zh: 」檜以諭燾，燾曰：「君命也，焉敢辭。

translations.literal: Hui relayed this to Dao, who said: "It is the ruler's command—how dare I refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui relayed this to Dao, who said: "It is the sovereign's command—how could I refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」十月，以寶文閣學士知成都府兼本路安撫使，付以便宜，雖安撫一路，而四川賦斂無藝者，悉得蠲減。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was appointed Hanlin academician of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Chengdu, concurrently pacification commissioner of the circuit, with discretionary authority. Though he pacified only one circuit, all exorbitant taxes and levies in Sichuan could be remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was made Hanlin academician of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Chengdu, concurrently circuit pacification commissioner, with discretionary authority. Though his jurisdiction was one circuit, he could remit all exorbitant taxes across Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，奏曰：「蜀民困矣，官吏從而誅剝之，去朝廷遠，無所赴。

translations.literal: At his audience of leave he memorialized: "The people of Shu are in distress, and officials follow by extorting and stripping them. Far from the court, they have nowhere to turn."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience he memorialized: "The people of Shu are suffering, and officials extort them further. Far from court, they have nowhere to turn."

sentences.zh: 俟臣至所部，首宣德意，但一路咸沾惠澤。

translations.literal: When your servant reaches his jurisdiction, he will first proclaim the imperial intent, so that the entire circuit may share in its beneficence.
translations.idiomatic: When I reach my post, I will first proclaim the imperial intent so the entire circuit may benefit.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「豈惟一路，四川恤民事悉委卿。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Not only one circuit—all relief of the people's affairs in Sichuan is entrusted to you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Not just one circuit—all relief for the people of Sichuan is entrusted to you."

sentences.zh: 」燾因言官吏害民者，請先罷後劾，上許之。

translations.literal: Dao then said that for officials who harm the people, he asked to dismiss them first and impeach them afterward. The emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: Dao asked that officials who harm the people be dismissed first and impeached afterward. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「軍興十餘年，日不暇給。

translations.literal: He also said: "War has been underway for more than ten years, and each day has left no time to spare."
translations.idiomatic: He also noted: "War has raged for more than ten years, leaving no time for anything else."

sentences.zh: 今和議甫定，願汲汲以政刑為先務。

translations.literal: Now that peace has just been settled, I hope Your Majesty will urgently make governance and punishments the first priority.
translations.idiomatic: Now that peace is settled, I urge Your Majesty to make governance and justice the top priority.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「當書之座右。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "This should be written at my right hand."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Write that at my right hand."

sentences.zh: 」十年三月，至成都。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year he reached Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year he arrived in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 在蜀四年，戢貪吏，薄租賦；

translations.literal: During four years in Shu he restrained corrupt officials and lightened taxes and levies;
translations.idiomatic: During four years in Shu he reined in corrupt officials and lightened taxes;

sentences.zh: 撫雅州蕃部，西邊不驚；

translations.literal: he pacified the tribal peoples of Yazhou, and the western frontier was undisturbed;
translations.idiomatic: he pacified the tribal peoples of Yazhou, keeping the western frontier quiet;

sentences.zh: 歲旱則發粟，民得不饑；

translations.literal: when drought came he distributed grain, so the people did not go hungry;
translations.idiomatic: in drought years he distributed grain so the people did not starve;

sentences.zh: 暇則修學校，與諸生講論。

translations.literal: in leisure he restored schools and lectured with the students.
translations.idiomatic: in quieter times he restored schools and lectured with students.

sentences.zh: 會有詔令宣撫司納契丹降人，燾為宣撫使胡世將言：「蜀地狹不能容，前朝常勝軍可為戒。

translations.literal: When an edict ordered the pacification commission to accept Khitan defectors, Dao spoke to Pacification Commissioner Hu Shijiang: "Shu territory is narrow and cannot contain them—the Changsheng Army of the previous dynasty should serve as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the pacification commission to accept Khitan defectors, Dao told Pacification Commissioner Hu Shijiang: "Shu is too narrow to hold them—the Changsheng Army of the previous dynasty should serve as warning enough."

sentences.zh: 」世將奏寢其事。

translations.literal: Shijiang memorialized to shelve the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiang memorialized to drop the matter.

sentences.zh: 燾乞祠，以李璆代之。

translations.literal: Dao requested a temple post and was replaced by Li Qiu.
translations.idiomatic: Dao requested a temple post and Li Qiu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 燾自蜀歸，臥家凡十有三年。

translations.literal: After Dao returned from Shu, he remained at home in retirement for thirteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from Shu, Dao lived in retirement at home for thirteen years.

sentences.zh: 二十五年冬，檜死，舊人在者皆起，燾除知建康府兼行宮留守。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-fifth year, when Hui died, all former associates still living were recalled; Dao was appointed prefect of Jiankang and concurrent keeper of the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the twenty-fifth year, when Hui died, former associates were recalled; Dao was made prefect of Jiankang and concurrent keeper of the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 金陵積歲負內庫錢帛鉅萬，悉為奏免。

translations.literal: Jinling had owed the inner treasury tens of thousands in cash and silk accumulated over years; he memorialized to have it all remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling owed the inner treasury tens of thousands in cash and silk accumulated over years; he memorialized to have it all forgiven.

sentences.zh: 池有義子與父爭訟，守昏謬，繫父，連年不決，燾移大理，斥其守。

translations.literal: In Chi there was an adopted son who sued his father. The prefect was muddle-headed, imprisoned the father, and left the case unresolved for years. Dao transferred it to the Court of Judicial Review and rebuked the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Chi an adopted son sued his father. The muddle-headed prefect imprisoned the father and left the case unresolved for years. Dao transferred it to the Court of Judicial Review and rebuked the prefect.

sentences.zh: 居二年，進端明殿學士。

translations.literal: After two years he was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，提舉萬壽觀兼侍讀，以衰疾力辭，不許。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was made superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey and concurrent reader-in-waiting. He forcefully declined on grounds of age and illness, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was made superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey and concurrent reader-in-waiting. He declined on grounds of age and illness but was refused.

sentences.zh: 除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 初，上知普安郡王賢，欲建為嗣，顯仁皇后意未欲，遲回久之。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor knew that Prince of Pu'an Commandery was worthy and wished to establish him as heir, but Empress Xianren was not yet willing, and the matter dragged on for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor knew the Prince of Pu'an was worthy and wished to make him heir, but Empress Xianren was not yet willing, and the matter dragged on.

sentences.zh: 顯仁崩，上問燾方今大計，燾曰：「儲貳者，國之本也，天下大計，無逾於此。

translations.literal: When Xianren died, the emperor asked Dao about the great plan of the present day. Dao said: "The heir apparent is the root of the state. No plan under Heaven exceeds this."
translations.idiomatic: When Xianren died, the emperor asked Dao about the great question of the day. Dao said: "The heir apparent is the root of the state. No national question exceeds this."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕懷此久矣，卿言契朕心，開春當議典禮。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have long harbored this thought. Your words match my heart. When spring opens we shall discuss the ritual ceremonies."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I have long had this in mind. Your words match my heart. When spring comes we shall discuss the ceremonies."

sentences.zh: 」又勸上省賜予，罷土木，減冗吏，止北貨。

translations.literal: He also urged the emperor to reduce grants and favors, halt construction projects, cut redundant officials, and stop northern goods.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged the emperor to cut grants, halt construction, reduce redundant officials, and stop importing northern goods.

sentences.zh: 上嘉獎之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him.

sentences.zh: 金使施宜生來，燾奉詔館客。

translations.literal: When the Jin envoy Shi Yisheng came, Dao was ordered by edict to serve as host.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin envoy Shi Yisheng arrived, Dao was ordered by edict to serve as his host.

sentences.zh: 宜生本閩人，素聞燾名，一見顧副使曰：「是南朝不拜詔者。

translations.literal: Yisheng was originally a man of Min and had long heard of Dao's name. At their first meeting he turned to the vice envoy and said: "This is the man of the Southern Court who refused to bow to the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Yisheng was originally from Min and had long heard of Dao. At their first meeting he turned to the vice envoy: "This is the Southern Court official who refused to bow to the edict."

sentences.zh: 」燾以「首丘桑梓」動之，宜生於是漏敵情，燾密奏早為備。

translations.literal: Dao moved him with talk of "returning one's head to the mound of one's native mulberry." Yisheng thereupon leaked enemy intelligence, and Dao secretly memorialized to prepare early.
translations.idiomatic: Dao appealed to him with talk of returning home to one's native soil. Yisheng then leaked enemy intelligence, and Dao secretly memorialized for early preparations.

sentences.zh: 先是，御前置甲庫，凡乘輿所需圖畫什物，有司不能供者悉聚焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, the imperial household had established an armor depot where all paintings and objects needed for the imperial carriage that the regular offices could not supply were gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the imperial household had established an armor depot where all paintings and objects for the imperial carriage that regular offices could not supply were gathered.

sentences.zh: 日費不貲。

translations.literal: Daily expenses were incalculable.
translations.idiomatic: Daily expenses were enormous.

sentences.zh: 禁中既有內酒庫，釀殊勝，酤賣其餘，頗侵大農。

translations.literal: Within the palace there was also an inner wine depot that brewed superior vintages and sold the surplus, considerably encroaching on the grand granary's revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace there was also an inner wine depot brewing superior vintages and selling the surplus, cutting into the grand granary's revenue.

sentences.zh: 燾因對，言甲庫萃工巧以蕩上心，酒庫酤良醞以奪官課。

translations.literal: Dao spoke on audience, saying the armor depot gathered artisans to corrupt the ruler's heart, and the wine depot sold fine brews to seize official tax revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Dao said the armor depot gathered artisans to corrupt the ruler's heart, and the wine depot sold fine brews to seize official tax revenue.

sentences.zh: 且乞罷減教坊樂工人數。

translations.literal: He also asked that the number of musicians in the Music Bureau be abolished or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the Music Bureau's musicians be abolished or reduced.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言可謂責難於君。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words may be called holding the ruler to difficult standards."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Your words hold the ruler to a difficult standard."

sentences.zh: 」明日悉詔罷之。

translations.literal: The next day edicts abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: The next day edicts abolished them all.

sentences.zh: 屢以衰疾乞骸。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested retirement on grounds of age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以資政殿學士致仕，尋遷太中大夫，給真奉。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he retired as Hanlin academician of the Zizheng Hall, and soon afterward was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Attendance with a stipend in kind.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he retired as Hanlin academician of the Zizheng Hall, and soon after was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Attendance with a stipend.

sentences.zh: 三十一年八月，落致仕，復知建康府。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the thirty-first year his retirement was revoked and he was again appointed prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the thirty-first year his retirement was revoked and he was again made prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 時金人窺江，建業民驚徙過半，聞燾至，人情稍安。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin were probing the Yangzi. More than half the people of Jianye fled in alarm, but when they heard Dao was coming, public sentiment calmed somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were probing the Yangzi. More than half the people of Jianye fled in alarm, but when they heard Dao was coming, public sentiment eased.

sentences.zh: 尋詔沿江帥臣條上恢復事宜，燾首陳十事，大率欲預備不虞，持重養威，觀釁而動，期於必勝。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered frontier commanders along the river to submit detailed plans for recovery. Dao was first to present ten items, generally aiming to prepare against the unexpected, hold weight and nurture prestige, watch for openings and act, and expect certain victory.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered river frontier commanders to submit recovery plans. Dao was first to present ten proposals, generally aiming to prepare for the unexpected, hold strength and nurture prestige, watch for openings, and fight to win.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，除同知樞密院，遣子埏入辭。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong received the abdication, Dao was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. He sent his son Yan to take leave on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, Dao was appointed vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. He sent his son Yan to take leave on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 詔肩輿至宮，給扶上殿，首問為治之要，言內治乃可外攘。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a sedan chair to bring him to the palace and supports to help him ascend the hall. The emperor first asked the essentials of governance; Dao said internal order must come before external resistance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a sedan chair to bring him to the palace with supports to help him ascend. The emperor first asked the essentials of governance; Dao said internal order must come before external resistance.

sentences.zh: 又乞命百執條弊事，詔從之，令侍從、臺諫集都堂給劄以聞。

translations.literal: He also asked that the hundred officials be ordered to list abuses. An edict agreed and ordered attendants and censorial remonstrators to gather at the chief council hall and submit memorials on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that all officials be ordered to list abuses. The throne agreed and ordered attendants and censorial officials to gather at the chief council hall and submit memorials.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，遷參知政事，以老病不拜，臺諫交章留之，除資政殿大學士、提舉萬壽觀兼侍讀。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing he was transferred to vice grand councilor but did not accept the appointment on grounds of age and illness. Censorial remonstrators submitted successive memorials asking him to stay, and he was made grand academician of the Zizheng Hall, superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey, and concurrent reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing he was transferred to vice grand councilor but declined on grounds of age and illness. Censorial officials submitted successive memorials asking him to stay, and he was made grand academician of the Zizheng Hall, superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey, and concurrent reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 謁告將理，許之。

translations.literal: He requested leave to tend to his affairs and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave to tend to personal affairs and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 及家，固求致仕。

translations.literal: When he reached home he firmly requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached home he firmly asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 後二年卒，年七十五，諡忠定。

translations.literal: Two years later he died at the age of seventy-five. His posthumous title was Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died at seventy-five. His posthumous title was Zhongding, "Loyal and Settled."

sentences.zh: 燾外和內剛，帥蜀有惠政，民祠之不忘。

translations.literal: Dao was outwardly mild and inwardly firm. As commander of Shu he enacted benevolent policies, and the people enshrined him and did not forget him.
translations.idiomatic: Dao was outwardly mild and inwardly firm. As commander of Shu he enacted benevolent policies, and the people enshrined him in memory.

sentences.zh: 始論和議，歸之於天，士論歉然。

translations.literal: When he first discussed the peace talks and attributed them to Heaven, scholarly opinion was dissatisfied.
translations.idiomatic: When he first discussed peace and attributed it to Heaven, scholarly opinion was dissatisfied.

sentences.zh: 洎繳駁施廷臣之奏，朝野復一辭歸重焉。

translations.literal: But when he rebutted Shi Tingchen's memorial, court and countryside again spoke with one voice in honoring him.
translations.idiomatic: But when he rebutted Shi Tingchen's memorial, court and country again spoke as one in honoring him.

sentences.zh: 黃中，字通老，邵武人。

translations.literal: Huang Zhong, courtesy name Tonglao, was a native of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhong, styled Tonglao, came from Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 幼受書，一再輒成誦。

translations.literal: As a child he studied books and could recite a text after reading it once or twice.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he studied the classics and could recite a text after one or two readings.

sentences.zh: 初以族祖蔭補官。

translations.literal: At first he received an official post through the yin privilege of a clan elder.
translations.idiomatic: At first he received an official post through a clan elder's yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年廷試，言孝弟動上心，擢進士第二人，授保寧軍節度推官。

translations.literal: In the palace examination of the fifth year of Shaoxing, his words on filial piety and brotherly respect moved the emperor's heart. He was placed second among jinshi and appointed military commissioner judge of the Baoning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace examination of the fifth year of Shaoxing, his words on filial piety and brotherly respect moved the emperor. He ranked second among jinshi and was appointed military commissioner judge of the Baoning Army.

sentences.zh: 二十餘年，秦檜死，乃召為校書郎，歷遷普安、恩平府教授。

translations.literal: For more than twenty years he remained in office. When Qin Hui died he was summoned as collator and successively transferred as instructor in Pu'an and Enping prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: For more than twenty years he remained in office. When Qin Hui died he was summoned as collator and later served as instructor in Pu'an and Enping prefectures.

sentences.zh: 中在王府時，龍大淵已親幸，中未嘗與之狎，見則揖而退，後他教授多蒙其力，中獨不徙官。

translations.literal: When Zhong was in the princely household, Long Dayuan was already a favorite, but Zhong never grew familiar with him—when they met he bowed and withdrew. Later many other instructors benefited from Dayuan's favor, but Zhong alone was not transferred.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong was in the princely household, Long Dayuan was already a favorite, but Zhong never grew familiar with him—when they met he bowed and withdrew. Later many instructors benefited from Dayuan's favor, but Zhong alone was never transferred.

sentences.zh: 遷司封員外郎兼國子司業。

translations.literal: He was transferred to outer-office director in the Ministry of Rites, concurrently vice director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to outer-office director in the Ministry of Rites, concurrently vice director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 芝草生武成廟，官吏請以聞，中不答，官吏陰畫圖以獻。

translations.literal: Lingzhi fungus grew at the Wucheng Temple. Officials asked to report it, but Zhong did not reply. The officials secretly painted a picture and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhi fungus appeared at the Wucheng Temple. Officials asked to report it, but Zhong did not reply. They secretly painted a picture and presented it.

sentences.zh: 宰相謂祭酒周綰與中曰：「治世之瑞，抑而不奏，何耶？

translations.literal: The chief minister said to Chancellor of the Directorate Zhou Wan and Zhong: "An auspicious sign in an age of good governance—why suppress it and not memorialize it?"
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister said to Chancellor Zhou Wan and Zhong: "An auspicious sign in an age of good governance—why suppress it and not report it?"

sentences.zh: 」綰未對，中曰：「治世何用此為？

translations.literal: Wan did not reply. Zhong said: "What use is this in an age of good governance?"
translations.idiomatic: Wan did not reply. Zhong said: "What use is this in an age of good governance?"

sentences.zh: 」綰退，謂人曰：「黃司業之言精切簡當，惜不為諫官。」

translations.literal: When Wan withdrew he said to others: "Vice Director Huang's words are precise, apt, and concise—it is a pity he is not a remonstrating official."
translations.idiomatic: When Wan withdrew he said: "Vice Director Huang's words are precise and apt—it is a pity he is not a remonstrating official."

sentences.zh: 充賀金生辰使，還，為秘書少監，尋除起居郎，累遷權禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served as envoy to congratulate the Jin ruler on his birthday. On his return he was made vice director of the Secretariat and soon appointed diarist-attendant, then successively promoted to acting vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served as envoy to congratulate the Jin ruler on his birthday. On return he was made vice director of the Secretariat, soon appointed diarist-attendant, and later promoted to acting vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 中使金回，言其治汴宮，必徙居見迫，宜早為計。

translations.literal: Zhong, returning from his mission to Jin, said they were renovating the Bian palace and would surely force a relocation—plans should be made early.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from his mission to Jin, Zhong said they were renovating the Bian palace and would surely force a relocation—plans should be made early.

sentences.zh: 上矍然。

translations.literal: The emperor started in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started in alarm.

sentences.zh: 宰相顧謂中曰：「沈介歸，殊不聞此，何耶？

translations.literal: The chief minister turned to Zhong and said: "When Shen Jie returned, he heard nothing of this—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister turned to Zhong: "When Shen Jie returned, he heard nothing of this—why?"

sentences.zh: 」居數日，中白宰相，請以妄言待罪。

translations.literal: After several days Zhong informed the chief minister and asked to await punishment for reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Zhong informed the chief minister and asked to await punishment for reckless speech.

sentences.zh: 湯思退怒，語侵中。

translations.literal: Tang Situi grew angry and his words insulted Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Situi grew angry and insulted Zhong.

sentences.zh: 已乃除介吏部侍郎，徙中以補其處。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jie was appointed vice minister of personnel and Zhong was transferred to fill his place.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jie was made vice minister of personnel and Zhong was transferred to fill his place.

sentences.zh: 中猶以備邊為言，又不聽，遂請補外，上不許，曰：「黃中恬退有守。

translations.literal: Zhong still spoke on frontier defense, but again was not heeded. He then requested an outer appointment, but the emperor did not permit it, saying: "Huang Zhong is calm, retiring, and principled."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong still spoke on frontier defense but was not heeded. He requested an outer appointment, but the emperor refused, saying: "Huang Zhong is calm, retiring, and principled."

sentences.zh: 」除左史，且錫鞍馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed left diarist and also granted a saddle and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed left diarist and granted a saddle and horse.

sentences.zh: 金使賀天申節，遽以欽宗訃聞，朝論俟使去發喪，中馳白宰相：「此國家大事，臣子至痛，一有失禮，謂天下後世何！

translations.literal: When a Jin envoy came to congratulate the Tianshen Festival, news of Emperor Qinzong's death was suddenly announced. Court opinion favored waiting until the envoy departed before proclaiming mourning. Zhong rushed to inform the chief minister: "This is a great affair of state and the deepest grief of a subject. One lapse in ritual—what would we say to the realm and posterity!"
translations.idiomatic: When a Jin envoy came for the Tianshen Festival, news of Emperor Qinzong's death was suddenly announced. Court opinion favored waiting until the envoy left before proclaiming mourning. Zhong rushed to the chief minister: "This is a great affair of state and the deepest grief of a subject. One lapse in ritual—what would we say to the realm and posterity!"

sentences.zh: 」竟得如禮。

translations.literal: In the end mourning was conducted according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the end mourning was conducted according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 中自使還，每進見，輒言邊事，又獨陳禦備方略，高宗稱善。

translations.literal: From the time Zhong returned from his mission, whenever he had audience he spoke on frontier affairs and alone presented strategies for defense. Emperor Gaozong praised him.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Zhong returned from his mission, whenever he had audience he spoke on frontier affairs and alone presented defense strategies. Emperor Gaozong praised him.

sentences.zh: 不數月，金亮已擁眾渡淮。

translations.literal: Within a few months, Jin's Prince Liang had already led his forces across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months, Jin's Prince Liang had already led his forces across the Huai.

sentences.zh: 中因入謝，論淮西將士不用命，請擇大臣督師。

translations.literal: Zhong then entered to give thanks and discussed how the Huai West generals and soldiers were not obeying orders, asking that a chief minister be chosen to supervise the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong then entered to give thanks and argued that Huai West troops were disobeying orders, asking that a senior minister be chosen to supervise the army.

sentences.zh: 既而以殿帥楊存中為御營使，中率同列力論不可遣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Palace Guard Commander Yang Cunzhong was made commissioner of the imperial camp. Zhong led his colleagues in forcefully arguing that he must not be dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yang Cunzhong, commander of the palace guard, was made commissioner of the imperial camp. Zhong led his colleagues in forcefully arguing that he must not be sent.

sentences.zh: 敵既臨江，朝臣爭遣家逃匿，中獨晏然。

translations.literal: Once the enemy reached the river, court ministers competed to send their families into hiding, but Zhong alone remained calm.
translations.idiomatic: Once the enemy reached the river, court ministers rushed to send their families into hiding, but Zhong alone remained calm.

sentences.zh: 比敵退，唯中與陳康伯家屬在城中，眾慚服。

translations.literal: When the enemy withdrew, only Zhong and Chen Kangbo's families remained in the city, and the multitude felt ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy withdrew, only Zhong and Chen Kangbo's families remained in the city, and others felt ashamed and submitted.

sentences.zh: 天申節上壽，議者以欽宗服除當舉樂。

translations.literal: At the Tianshen Festival birthday celebration, debaters held that since mourning for Emperor Qinzong had ended, music should be performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Tianshen Festival birthday celebration, some argued that since mourning for Emperor Qinzong had ended, music should be performed.

sentences.zh: 中言：「《春秋》君弑賊不討，雖葬不書，以明臣子之罪，況欽宗實未葬而可遽作樂乎？

translations.literal: Zhong said: "In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a ruler was murdered and the killer was not punished, even burial was not recorded—to show the guilt of ministers and subjects. How much less can music be hastily performed when Qinzong has in fact not yet been buried?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: "In the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a ruler was murdered and the killer went unpunished, even burial went unrecorded—to show the guilt of ministers and subjects. How can we hastily perform music when Qinzong has not even been buried?"

sentences.zh: 」事竟寢。

translations.literal: The matter was ultimately shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 兼給事中。

translations.literal: He was concurrently appointed supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was concurrently made supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 內侍遷官不應法，諫官劉度坐論近習龍大淵忤旨補郡，已復罷之，中皆不書讀。

translations.literal: Eunuchs were promoted in violation of law. Remonstrating official Liu Du was punished for criticizing the favorite Long Dayuan and assigned to a prefecture, then dismissed again—Zhong refused to endorse any of these edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs were promoted illegally. Remonstrating official Liu Du was punished for criticizing favorite Long Dayuan and sent to a prefecture, then dismissed again—Zhong refused to endorse any of these edicts.

sentences.zh: 群小相與媒蘖，中罷去。

translations.literal: Petty men banded together to slander him, and Zhong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men banded together to slander him, and Zhong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尹穡希意詆中為張浚黨。

translations.literal: Yin Ji, seeking favor, slandered Zhong as a member of Zhang Jun's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ji, seeking favor, slandered Zhong as a Zhang Jun partisan.

sentences.zh: 乾道改元，中年適七十，即告老，以集英殿修撰致仕，進敷文閣待制。

translations.literal: When the reign title was changed to Qiandao, Zhong happened to be seventy and immediately requested retirement. He retired as Hanlin academician compiler of the Jiying Hall and was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Fuwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title changed to Qiandao, Zhong turned seventy and immediately retired as Hanlin academician compiler of the Jiying Hall, then was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Fuwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 居六年，上御講筵，顧侍臣曰：「黃中老儒，今居何許？

translations.literal: After six years at home, the emperor presided over the lecture hall and turned to his attendants, saying: "The old scholar Huang Zhong—where does he live now?"
translations.idiomatic: After six years at home, the emperor presided over the lecture hall and asked his attendants: "The old scholar Huang Zhong—where does he live now?"

sentences.zh: 年幾許？

translations.literal: How old is he?
translations.idiomatic: How old is he?

sentences.zh: 筋力或未衰耶？
