translations.literal: Perhaps his strength has not yet declined?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps his strength has not yet failed?

sentences.zh: 」召引對內殿，問勞甚渥，以為兵部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: He was summoned for an audience in the inner hall and questioned with great kindness. He was appointed minister of war and concurrent reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to audience in the inner hall and questioned with great kindness. He was made minister of war and concurrent reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 中前在禮部，嘗諫止作樂事，中去，卒用之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhong was in the Ministry of Rites, he had remonstrated against performing music. After Zhong left, music was ultimately used.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhong was in the Ministry of Rites, he had remonstrated against performing music. After he left, music was performed anyway.

sentences.zh: 至是又將錫宴，遂奏申前說。

translations.literal: Now a banquet was again to be granted, so he memorialized restating his earlier view.
translations.idiomatic: Now a banquet was to be granted again, so he memorialized restating his earlier view.

sentences.zh: 詔遣范成大使金以山陵為請。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Fan Chengda as envoy to Jin to request the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict dispatched Fan Chengda as envoy to Jin to request return of the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 中言：「陛下聖孝及此，天下幸甚，然欽廟梓宮置不問，有所未盡。

translations.literal: Zhong said: "Your Majesty's sacred filial piety reaches this far—the realm is greatly fortunate. Yet Emperor Qinzong's coffin in the ancestral temple is left unaddressed; something remains incomplete."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said: "Your Majesty's filial devotion reaches this far—the realm is greatly fortunate. Yet Emperor Qinzong's coffin is left unaddressed; something remains incomplete."

sentences.zh: 」上善其言，不能用。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of his words but could not adopt them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved of his words but could not act on them.

sentences.zh: 未滿歲，有歸志，乃陳十要道：以為用人而不自用；

translations.literal: Before a full year had passed he wished to return home and presented ten essential points: that the ruler should employ men but not rely on others to decide for himself;
translations.idiomatic: Before a full year had passed he wished to return home and presented ten essential points: employ men but decide for yourself;

sentences.zh: 以公議進退人才；

translations.literal: advance and dismiss talent according to public opinion;
translations.idiomatic: advance and dismiss talent by public opinion;

sentences.zh: 察邪正；

translations.literal: discern the wicked from the upright;
translations.idiomatic: discern wicked from upright;

sentences.zh: 廣言路；

translations.literal: broaden channels for speech;
translations.idiomatic: broaden channels for free speech;

sentences.zh: 核事實；

translations.literal: verify facts;
translations.idiomatic: verify facts;

sentences.zh: 節用度；

translations.literal: economize expenditures;
translations.idiomatic: economize spending;

sentences.zh: 擇監司；

translations.literal: choose circuit intendants carefully;
translations.idiomatic: choose circuit intendants carefully;

sentences.zh: 懲貪吏；

translations.literal: punish corrupt officials;
translations.idiomatic: punish corrupt officials;

sentences.zh: 陳方略；

translations.literal: set forth strategy;
translations.idiomatic: set forth strategy;

sentences.zh: 考兵籍。

translations.literal: and examine military registers.
translations.idiomatic: and examine military registers.

sentences.zh: 上亟稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor quickly praised this as excellent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quickly praised this.

sentences.zh: 中力求去，除顯謨閣、提舉江州太平興國宮，賜犀帶、香茗。

translations.literal: Zhong forcefully sought to leave and was made Hanlin academician of the Xianmo Pavilion and superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey in Jiangzhou, granted a rhinoceros-horn belt and fragrant tea.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong forcefully sought to leave and was made Hanlin academician of the Xianmo Pavilion and superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Abbey at Jiangzhou, granted a rhinoceros-horn belt and fragrant tea.

sentences.zh: 除龍圖閣學士，致仕。

translations.literal: He was made Hanlin academician of the Longtu Pavilion and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Hanlin academician of the Longtu Pavilion and retired.

sentences.zh: 凡邑里後生上謁，必訓以孝弟忠信。

translations.literal: Whenever young men of the locality came to pay respects, he always instructed them in filial piety, brotherly respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever young men of the locality came to visit, he always instructed them in filial piety, brotherly respect, loyalty, and trustworthiness.

sentences.zh: 朱熹裁書以見，有曰：「今日之來，將再拜堂下，惟公坐而受之，俾進于門弟子之列，則某之志也。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi wrote a letter to visit him, saying: "In coming today I intend to bow twice in your hall. I ask only that you sit and receive me, allowing me to enter the ranks of your disciples at the gate—this is my wish."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi wrote to visit him, saying: "In coming today I intend to bow twice in your hall. I ask only that you sit and receive me, allowing me to enter the ranks of your disciples—this is my wish."

sentences.zh: 」其為人敬慕如此。

translations.literal: Such was the reverence and admiration his character inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the reverence his character inspired.

sentences.zh: 其後，上手書遣使訪朝政闕失，進職端明殿學士。

translations.literal: Later the emperor personally wrote and dispatched envoys to inquire about failures in court governance, and Zhong was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Duanming Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor personally wrote and dispatched envoys to inquire about failures in court governance, and Zhong was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Duanming Hall.

sentences.zh: 屬疾，手草遺表，猶以山陵、欽宗梓宮為言，深以人主之職不可假之左右為戒。

translations.literal: When illness came upon him, he personally drafted a final memorial, still speaking of the imperial tombs and Emperor Qinzong's coffin, deeply warning that the sovereign's duties must not be entrusted to those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When illness came upon him, he personally drafted a final memorial, still speaking of the imperial tombs and Emperor Qinzong's coffin, deeply warning that the sovereign's duties must not be entrusted to those at his side.

sentences.zh: 淳熙七年八月庚寅卒，年八十有五。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the seventh year of Chunxi, on the gengyin day, he died at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the seventh year of Chunxi, on the gengyin day, he died at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 九月，詔贈正議大夫。

translations.literal: In the ninth month an edict posthumously granted him the title Righteous Discussion Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month an edict posthumously granted him the title Righteous Discussion Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 中有奏議十卷。

translations.literal: Zhong left ten fascicles of memorials and proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong left ten fascicles of memorials and proposals.

sentences.zh: 諡「簡肅」。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was "Simple and Stern."
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Jiansu, "Simple and Stern."

sentences.zh: 孫道夫

translations.literal: Sun Daofu
translations.idiomatic: Sun Daofu

sentences.zh: 孫道夫，字太沖，眉州丹棱人。

translations.literal: Sun Daofu, courtesy name Taichong, was a native of Danling in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Daofu, styled Taichong, came from Danling in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 年十八貢辟雍。

translations.literal: At eighteen he submitted tribute to the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he submitted tribute to the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 時禁元祐學，坐收蘇氏文除籍。

translations.literal: At that time Yuanyou learning was banned. He was punished for possessing Su-family writings and removed from the register.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuanyou learning was banned. He was punished for possessing Su-family writings and removed from the register.

sentences.zh: 再貢，入優等。

translations.literal: He submitted tribute again and entered the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted tribute again and entered the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 張浚薦于高宗，召對，道夫奏：「願修德以回天意，定都以繫人心，任賢材、圖興復以雪國恥。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jun recommended him to Emperor Gaozong. Summoned for audience, Daofu memorialized: "I wish to cultivate virtue to turn back Heaven's intent, establish the capital to bind people's hearts, employ worthy talent, and plan restoration to wipe away the nation's shame."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun recommended him to Emperor Gaozong. Summoned to audience, Daofu memorialized: "Cultivate virtue to turn Heaven's intent, establish the capital to bind hearts, employ worthy talent, and plan restoration to wipe away national shame."

sentences.zh: 上在越，浚遣道夫奏事，賜出身，改左承奉郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was in Yue. Jun sent Daofu to report affairs and he was granted official standing, changing to Left Assistant Gentleman for Court Service.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was in Yue. Jun sent Daofu to report affairs and he was granted official standing, becoming Left Assistant Gentleman for Court Service.

sentences.zh: 再詔對，言：「漢中前瞰三秦，後蔽巴蜀，孔明、蔣琬出圖關輔，未有不屯漢中者。

translations.literal: Again summoned for audience, he said: "Hanzhong looks out over the Three Qins in front and shields Ba and Shu behind. When Kongming and Jiang Wan marched out toward the Guanzhong region, they never failed to encamp at Hanzhong."
translations.idiomatic: Again summoned to audience, he said: "Hanzhong looks out over the Three Qins and shields Ba and Shu. When Kongming and Jiang Wan marched toward Guanzhong, they always encamped at Hanzhong."

sentences.zh: 今欲進兵陝右，當先經營漢中。

translations.literal: If we now wish to advance troops into the right of Shaanxi, we should first establish Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: If we now wish to advance into western Shaanxi, we should first establish Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 荊南東連吳會，北通漢沔，號用武之國，晉、宋以來，嘗倚為重鎮。

translations.literal: Jingnan connects east to Wu and Kuaiji and north to Han and Mian. It is called a land for wielding force. Since Jin and Song times it has often been relied upon as a strategic stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan connects east to Wu and Kuaiji and north to Han and Mian. Called a land for wielding force, since Jin and Song times it has been relied upon as a strategic stronghold.

sentences.zh: 武帝亦以荊南居上流，故以諸子居之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin also placed his sons there because Jingnan lay on the upper reaches.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin also placed his sons there because Jingnan lay on the upper reaches.

sentences.zh: 今守江當先措置荊南，時至則蜀漢師出秦關，荊楚師出宛洛，陛下親御六軍，由淮甸與諸將會咸陽，孰能禦之？

translations.literal: Today in defending the river we should first arrange Jingnan. When the time comes, Shu-Han armies will march out through Qin Pass, Jing-Chu armies out through Wan and Luoyang, and Your Majesty will personally lead the six armies from the Huai region to join the generals at Xianyang—who could withstand us?
translations.idiomatic: Today in defending the river we should first secure Jingnan. When the time comes, Shu armies will march through Qin Pass, Jing-Chu armies through Wan and Luoyang, and Your Majesty will lead the six armies from the Huai to join generals at Xianyang—who could withstand us?

sentences.zh: 」上嘉納，召試館職。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this and summoned him for an examination for an academy post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted this and summoned him for an academy examination.

sentences.zh: 上諭宰相：「自渡江以來，文氣未有如道夫者，涵養一二年，當命為詞臣。」

translations.literal: The emperor told the chief minister: "Since crossing the river, no literary talent has matched Daofu. After nurturing him for a year or two, he should be appointed a drafting official."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chief minister: "Since crossing the river, no literary talent has matched Daofu. After nurturing him a year or two, he should be appointed a drafting official."

sentences.zh: 除秘書正字、權禮部郎官。

translations.literal: He was appointed proofreader in the Secretariat and acting director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretariat proofreader and acting director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 徽宗凶問禮儀，多所草定。

translations.literal: He drafted much of the ritual for announcing Emperor Huizong's death.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted much of the ritual for announcing Emperor Huizong's death.

sentences.zh: 尋權左司員外郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made acting outer-office director in the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was made acting outer-office director in the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 上問蜀中水運陸運孰便？

translations.literal: The emperor asked which was more convenient in Shu, transport by water or by land.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked which was more convenient in Shu, transport by water or by land.

sentences.zh: 道夫奏：「水運遲而省費，陸運速而勞民。

translations.literal: Daofu memorialized: "Water transport is slow but saves expense; land transport is fast but burdens the people."
translations.idiomatic: Daofu memorialized: "Water transport is slow but saves expense; land transport is fast but burdens the people."

sentences.zh: 宣撫司初由水運，率石費錢十千，後以為緩，從陸起丁夫十數萬，率石費五十餘千。

translations.literal: The pacification commission at first used water transport, costing about ten thousand cash per shi of grain. Later, finding it too slow, they used land transport and drafted several hundred thousand corvée laborers, costing more than fifty thousand cash per shi.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification commission at first used water transport at about ten thousand cash per shi. Later, finding it too slow, they used land transport with several hundred thousand corvée laborers at more than fifty thousand cash per shi.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「水運便，行之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Water transport is convenient—use it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Water transport is convenient—use it."

sentences.zh: 遷校書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to collator.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to collator.

sentences.zh: 出知懷安軍，乞罷都運司以寬民力，罷戍兵以弭亂階，罷泛使以省浮費。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Huai'an Army and requested abolishing the transport commission to ease the people's burden, abolishing garrison troops to remove seeds of disorder, and abolishing general envoys to cut unnecessary expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Huai'an Army and requested abolishing the transport commission to ease the people's burden, abolishing garrison troops to remove seeds of disorder, and abolishing general envoys to cut unnecessary expenses.

sentences.zh: 知資州，宣撫鄭剛中薦其治行第一。

translations.literal: As prefect of Zizhou, Pacification Commissioner Zheng Gangzhong recommended his governance as first rank.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Zizhou, Pacification Commissioner Zheng Gangzhong recommended his governance as first rank.

sentences.zh: 移知蜀州，盜不敢入境。

translations.literal: Transferred as prefect of Shuzhou, bandits did not dare enter his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred as prefect of Shuzhou, bandits did not dare enter his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 州產綾，先是，守以軍匠置機買絲虧直，民病之，道夫斷其機。

translations.literal: The prefecture produced gauze. Previously the prefect had used military artisans to set up looms, buying silk below market price to the people's distress. Daofu shut down the looms.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture produced gauze. Previously the prefect had military artisans set up looms, buying silk below market price to the people's distress. Daofu shut down the looms.

sentences.zh: 遇事明瞭，人目為「水晶燈籠」。

translations.literal: He was clear in handling affairs, and people called him a "crystal lantern."
translations.idiomatic: He was clear in handling affairs, and people called him a "crystal lantern."

sentences.zh: 九年不遷，蓋非秦檜所樂也。

translations.literal: For nine years he received no promotion—this was surely not to Qin Hui's liking.
translations.idiomatic: For nine years he received no promotion—surely not to Qin Hui's liking.

sentences.zh: 以吏部郎中入對，言蜀民二稅監酒茶額之弊，上納其言。

translations.literal: Entering audience as director in the Ministry of Personnel, he spoke of abuses in the two taxes, wine monopoly, and tea quotas burdening Shu people. The emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Entering audience as director in the Ministry of Personnel, he spoke of abuses in the two taxes, wine monopoly, and tea quotas burdening Shu people. The emperor accepted his words.

sentences.zh: 除太常少卿，假禮部侍郎充賀金正旦使。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting vice minister of rites as envoy to congratulate Jin on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and acting vice minister of rites as envoy to congratulate Jin on New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 金將敗盟，詰秦檜存亡，及關、陝買馬非約，道夫隨事折之。

translations.literal: The Jin were about to break the treaty. They questioned whether Qin Hui still lived and whether buying horses in Guan and Shaanxi was not in the agreement. Daofu rebutted each point as it arose.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were about to break the treaty. They questioned whether Qin Hui still lived and whether buying horses in Guan and Shaanxi violated the agreement. Daofu rebutted each point as it arose.

sentences.zh: 使還，擢權禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: On his return from the mission he was promoted to acting vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: On return from the mission he was promoted to acting vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿自小官已為朕知，第趙鼎與張浚相失後，蜀士仕於朝者，皆為沮抑。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I have known you since you were a minor official. But after Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun fell out, Shu scholars serving at court were all suppressed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I have known you since you were a minor official. But after Zhao Ding and Zhang Jun fell out, Shu scholars at court were all suppressed."

sentences.zh: 繼自今有所見，可數求對。」

translations.literal: "From now on, whenever you have a view, you may frequently request audience."
translations.idiomatic: "From now on, whenever you have a view, you may frequently request audience."

sentences.zh: 兼侍講，奏敵有窺江、淮意。

translations.literal: Concurrently appointed lecturer-in-waiting, he memorialized that the enemy intended to probe the Yangzi and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Concurrently appointed lecturer-in-waiting, he memorialized that the enemy intended to probe the Yangzi and Huai.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朝廷待之甚厚，彼以何名為兵端？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The court has treated them very generously—under what pretext would they start hostilities?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The court has treated them very generously—under what pretext would they start hostilities?"

sentences.zh: 」道夫曰：「彼金人身弑其父兄而奪其位，興兵豈問有名，臣願預為之圖。

translations.literal: Daofu said: "That Jin prince murdered his father and elder brother to seize the throne—when raising armies does he ask for a pretext? Your servant wishes to plan ahead."
translations.idiomatic: Daofu said: "That Jin prince murdered his father and brother to seize the throne—when raising armies does he need a pretext? I wish to plan ahead."

sentences.zh: 」宰相沈該不以為慮，道夫每進對，輒言武事，該疑其引用張浚，忌之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Shen Gai did not consider this a concern. Whenever Daofu had audience he spoke of military affairs. Gai suspected he was invoking Zhang Jun and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Shen Gai did not consider this a concern. Whenever Daofu had audience he spoke of military affairs. Gai suspected he was invoking Zhang Jun and resented him.

sentences.zh: 道夫不自安，請出，除知綿州，致仕，卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: Daofu felt ill at ease and requested an outer appointment. He was made prefect of Mianzhou, retired, and died at the age of sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu felt ill at ease and requested an outer appointment. He was made prefect of Mianzhou, retired, and died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 道夫居官，一意為民，不可干以私。

translations.literal: In office Daofu devoted himself entirely to the people and could not be approached with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: In office Daofu devoted himself entirely to the people and could not be approached with private requests.

sentences.zh: 仕宦三十年，奉給多置書籍。

translations.literal: During thirty years of official service he spent most of his salary on books.
translations.idiomatic: During thirty years of official service he spent most of his salary on books.

sentences.zh: 然性剛直，喜面折，不容人之短，或以此少之云。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was stern and upright. He liked to confront people directly and would not tolerate others' faults—some therefore thought less of him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature was stern and upright. He liked to confront people directly and would not tolerate others' faults—some therefore thought less of him for this.

sentences.zh: 曾幾，字吉甫，其先贛州人，徙河南府。

translations.literal: Ceng Ji, courtesy name Jifu, was originally from Ganzhou and moved to Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng Ji, styled Jifu, was originally from Ganzhou and moved to Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼有識度，事親孝，母死，蔬食十五年。

translations.literal: As a child he had judgment and breadth. He was filial to his parents. When his mother died he ate plain food for fifteen years.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he showed judgment and breadth. He was filial to his parents. When his mother died he ate plain food for fifteen years.

sentences.zh: 入太學有聲。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University with a reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University with a reputation.

sentences.zh: 兄弼，提舉京西南路學事，按部溺死，無後，特命幾將仕郎。

translations.literal: His elder brother Bi, commissioner of learning for the Jingxi South Circuit, drowned while on inspection tour and left no heirs. Ji was specially appointed Gentleman for Initial Service.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Bi, commissioner of learning for the Jingxi South Circuit, drowned on inspection tour and left no heirs. Ji was specially appointed Gentleman for Initial Service.

sentences.zh: 試吏部，考官異其文，置優等，賜上舍出身，擢國子正兼欽慈皇后宅教授。

translations.literal: Examined by the Ministry of Personnel, the examiners found his essays exceptional and placed him in the highest grade. He was granted upper-hall standing and promoted to director of the Directorate of Education, concurrently instructor in the Empress Qinci's household.
translations.idiomatic: Examined by the Ministry of Personnel, examiners found his essays exceptional and placed him in the highest grade. He was granted upper-hall standing and promoted to director of the Directorate of Education, concurrently instructor in the Empress Qinci's household.

sentences.zh: 遷辟雍博士，除校書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to lecturer at the Imperial University and appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to lecturer at the Imperial University and appointed collator.

sentences.zh: 林靈素得幸，作符書號《神霄錄》，朝士爭趨之，幾與李綱、傅崧卿皆稱疾不往視。

translations.literal: Lin Lingsu gained favor and wrote talismanic texts titled Record of the Divine Empyrean. Court gentlemen competed to attend him. Ji, along with Li Gang and Fu Songqing, all pleaded illness and did not go to view them.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Lingsu gained favor and wrote talismanic texts titled Record of the Divine Empyrean. Court gentlemen competed to attend him. Ji, along with Li Gang and Fu Songqing, all pleaded illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 久之，為應天少尹，庭無留訟。

translations.literal: After a long time he became vice prefect of Yingtian. No lawsuits remained pending in his court.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he became vice prefect of Yingtian. No lawsuits remained pending in his court.

sentences.zh: 閹人得旨取金而無文書，府尹徐處仁與之，幾力爭不得。

translations.literal: A eunuch received an oral order to take gold without documentation. Prefect Xu Churen gave it to him, but Ji forcefully argued and could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch received an oral order to take gold without documentation. Prefect Xu Churen gave it to him, but Ji forcefully argued and could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 檜死，起為浙西提刑、知台州，治尚清淨，民安之。

translations.literal: When Hui died he was recalled as judicial intendant of Zhe West and prefect of Taizhou. His governance favored simplicity and quiet, and the people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui died he was recalled as judicial intendant of Zhe West and prefect of Taizhou. His governance favored simplicity and quiet, and the people were at ease.

sentences.zh: 黃岩令受賄為兩吏所持，令械吏置獄，一夕皆死，幾詰其罪。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Huangyan took bribes and was caught by two clerks. The magistrate shackled the clerks and imprisoned them; both died in one night. Ji investigated his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Huangyan took bribes and was caught by two clerks. The magistrate shackled the clerks and imprisoned them; both died in one night. Ji investigated his crime.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「令，丞相沈該客也。

translations.literal: Some said: "The magistrate is a client of Chief Minister Shen Gai."
translations.idiomatic: Some said: "The magistrate is a client of Chief Minister Shen Gai."

sentences.zh: 」治之益急。

translations.literal: Ji pursued the case all the more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Ji pursued the case all the more urgently.

sentences.zh: 賀允中薦，召對，以疾辭，除直秘閣，歸故治。

translations.literal: Recommended by He Yunzhong, he was summoned for audience but declined on grounds of illness. He was appointed direct access to the Secretariat and returned to his former jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by He Yunzhong, he was summoned for audience but declined on grounds of illness. He was appointed direct access to the Secretariat and returned to his former jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復召對，幾言：「士氣久不振，陛下欲起之於一朝，矯枉者必過直，雖有折檻斷鞅、牽裾還笏、若賣直干譽者，願加優容。

translations.literal: Before long he was again summoned for audience. Ji said: "Scholarly morale has long been depressed. Your Majesty wishes to revive it in a single day—those who overcorrect inevitably go too far. Even if some break the railing, snap the bridle, seize the robe, or return the tablet, or seem to sell integrity for reputation, I hope they may be treated with generous tolerance."
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again summoned for audience. Ji said: "Scholarly morale has long been depressed. Your Majesty wishes to revive it in a single day—those who overcorrect go too far. Even if some break the railing, snap the bridle, seize the robe, or return the tablet, or seem to sell integrity for reputation, I hope they may be treated with generous tolerance."

sentences.zh: 」時帝懲檜擅權之弊，方開言路，應詔者眾，幾懼有獲戾者，先事陳之。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor, mindful of the abuses of Hui's monopolization of power, was opening channels for speech. Many responded to edicts. Ji feared some might give offense and stated this in advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, mindful of Hui's monopolization of power, was opening channels for speech. Many responded to edicts. Ji feared some might give offense and stated this in advance.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，授秘書少監。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and appointed him vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and appointed him vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 幾承平已為館職，去三十八年而復至，鬚鬢皓白，衣冠偉然。

translations.literal: Ji had already held an academy post in peaceful times. After thirty-eight years he returned, his beard and hair snow-white, his bearing and dress imposing.
translations.idiomatic: Ji had already held an academy post in peaceful times. After thirty-eight years he returned, his hair snow-white, his bearing imposing.

sentences.zh: 每會同舍，多談前輩言行、臺閣典章，薦紳推重焉。

translations.literal: Whenever he met fellow academy members he often spoke of the conduct and words of earlier generations and the regulations of the secretariat. Gentry and officials held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he met fellow academy members he often spoke of earlier generations and secretariat regulations. Gentry and officials held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 詔修《神宗寶訓》，書成，奏薦，帝稱善。

translations.literal: An edict ordered compilation of the Precious Instructions of Emperor Shenzong. When the book was completed he memorialized with recommendations and the emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered compilation of the Precious Instructions of Emperor Shenzong. When the book was completed he memorialized with recommendations and the emperor praised it.

sentences.zh: 權禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was made acting vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 兄楙、開皆嘗貳春官，幾復為之，人以為榮。

translations.literal: His elder brothers Mao and Kai had both served as vice directors of the Ministry of Rites. Ji held the post again, and people regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brothers Mao and Kai had both served as vice directors of the Ministry of Rites. Ji held the post again, and people regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 吳、越大水、地震，幾舉唐貞元故事反覆論奏，帝韙其言。

translations.literal: Wu and Yue suffered great floods and earthquakes. Ji cited Tang precedents from the Zhenyuan era and memorialized repeatedly. The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Yue suffered great floods and earthquakes. Ji cited Tang precedents from the Zhenyuan era and memorialized repeatedly. The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 他日謂幾曰：「前所進陸贄事甚切，已遣漕臣振濟矣。

translations.literal: Another day he said to Ji: "Your earlier memorial on Lu Zhi was very apt. I have already dispatched transport officials to provide relief."
translations.idiomatic: Another day he said to Ji: "Your earlier memorial on Lu Zhi was very apt. I have already dispatched transport officials to provide relief."

sentences.zh: 」引年請謝，上曰：「卿氣貌不類老人，姑為朕留。

translations.literal: Citing his age he requested leave to retire. The emperor said: "Your bearing does not resemble an old man's—stay for now on my behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Citing his age he requested leave to retire. The emperor said: "Your bearing does not resemble an old man's—stay for now on my behalf."

sentences.zh: 」謝曰：「臣無補萬一，惟進退有禮，尚不負陛下拔擢。

translations.literal: He thanked him and said: "Your servant has been of no use whatsoever. Only in advancing and retiring with propriety have I not failed Your Majesty's elevation."
translations.idiomatic: He thanked him and said: "I have been of no use whatsoever. Only in advancing and retiring with propriety have I not failed Your Majesty's elevation."

sentences.zh: 」上閔勞以事，提舉玉隆觀，紹興二十七年也。

translations.literal: The emperor sympathized and reassured him with duties, making him superintendent of the Yulong Abbey. This was in the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sympathized and reassured him with duties, making him superintendent of the Yulong Abbey. This was in the twenty-seventh year of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 除集英殿修撰，又三年，升敷文閣待制。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin academician compiler of the Jiying Hall. Three years later he was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Fuwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin academician compiler of the Jiying Hall. Three years later he was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Fuwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 金犯塞，中外大震，帝召楊存中偕宰執對便殿，諭以將散百官，浮海避之。

translations.literal: The Jin violated the frontier and court and countryside were greatly shaken. The emperor summoned Yang Cunzhong together with the chief ministers to audience in the side hall and instructed them that he would dismiss the officials and flee by sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin violated the frontier and court and country were greatly shaken. The emperor summoned Yang Cunzhong and the chief ministers to audience in the side hall and said he would dismiss the officials and flee by sea.

sentences.zh: 左僕射陳康伯持不可。

translations.literal: Left Grand Counselor Chen Kangbo held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Left Grand Counselor Chen Kangbo held that this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 存中言：「敵空國遠來，已闖淮甸，此正賢智馳騖不足之時。

translations.literal: Cunzhong said: "The enemy has emptied their country to come from afar and has already broken into the Huai region. This is precisely the time when worthies and the wise cannot do enough."
translations.idiomatic: Cunzhong said: "The enemy has emptied their country to come from afar and has already broken into the Huai region. This is precisely when worthies and the wise must do all they can."

sentences.zh: 臣願率先將士，北首死敵。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to lead the generals and soldiers, turning north to die fighting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to lead the generals and soldiers, turning north to die fighting the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」帝喜，遂定議親征，下詔進討。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and thereupon decided on a personal campaign, issuing an edict to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and decided on a personal campaign, issuing an edict to advance and attack.

sentences.zh: 有欲遣使詣敵求緩師者，幾疏言：「增幣請和，無小益，有大害，為朝廷計，正當嘗膽枕戈，專務節儉，經武外一切置之，如是雖北取中原可也。

translations.literal: Some wished to dispatch envoys to the enemy to request a delay in hostilities. Ji memorialized: "Increasing tribute to seek peace brings no small benefit but great harm. For the court's sake we should sleep on brushwood and taste gall, devote ourselves solely to frugality, and set aside everything except military preparedness—then even recovering the Central Plain in the north would be possible."
translations.idiomatic: Some wished to dispatch envoys to request a delay in hostilities. Ji memorialized: "Increasing tribute to seek peace brings no small benefit but great harm. The court should sleep on brushwood and taste gall, devote itself solely to frugality, and set aside everything except military preparedness—then even recovering the Central Plain would be possible."

sentences.zh: 且前日詔諸將傳檄數金君臣，如叱奴隸，何辭可與之和耶？

translations.literal: Moreover, the other day an edict ordered the generals to circulate a proclamation denouncing the Jin ruler and ministers like scolding slaves—what words could we use to make peace with them?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the other day an edict ordered the generals to circulate a proclamation denouncing the Jin ruler and ministers like scolding slaves—what words could we use to make peace with them?

sentences.zh: 」帝壯之。

translations.literal: The emperor was heartened by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was heartened by this.

sentences.zh: 孝宗受禪，幾又上疏數千言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong received the abdication, Ji again submitted a memorial of several thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong received the abdication, Ji again submitted a memorial of several thousand words.

sentences.zh: 將召，屢請老，乃遷通奉大夫，致仕，擢其子逮為浙西提刑以便養。

translations.literal: About to be summoned, he repeatedly requested retirement on grounds of age. He was transferred to Grand Master for Court Audience and retired. His son Dai was promoted to judicial intendant of Zhe West to facilitate his care.
translations.idiomatic: About to be summoned, he repeatedly requested retirement on grounds of age. He was transferred to Grand Master for Court Audience and retired. His son Dai was promoted to judicial intendant of Zhe West to facilitate his care.

sentences.zh: 乾道二年卒，年八十二，諡「文清」。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Qiandao at the age of eighty-two. His posthumous title was "Literary and Pure."
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Qiandao at eighty-two. His posthumous title was Wenqing, "Literary and Pure."

sentences.zh: 幾三仕嶺表，家無長物，人稱其廉。

translations.literal: Ji served three times south of the Ling range and kept no surplus possessions at home. People praised his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Ji served three times south of the Ling range and kept no surplus possessions at home. People praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 早從舅氏孔文仲、武仲講學。

translations.literal: Early on he studied under his maternal uncles Kong Wenzhong and Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Early on he studied under his maternal uncles Kong Wenzhong and Wuzhong.

sentences.zh: 初佐應天時，諫官劉安世亡恙，黨禁方厲，無敢窺其門者，幾獨從之，談經論事，與之合。

translations.literal: When he first served as assistant in Yingtian, remonstrating official Liu Anshi was unharmed but factional bans were severe and none dared approach his door. Ji alone followed him, discussing the classics and affairs of state, and they agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When he first served as assistant in Yingtian, remonstrating official Liu Anshi was unharmed but factional bans were severe and none dared approach his door. Ji alone followed him, discussing the classics and affairs of state, and they agreed.

sentences.zh: 避地衡嶽，又從胡安國遊，其學益粹。

translations.literal: Taking refuge at Mount Heng, he also associated with Hu Anguo, and his learning grew more refined.
translations.idiomatic: Taking refuge at Mount Heng, he also associated with Hu Anguo, and his learning grew more refined.

sentences.zh: 為文純正雅健，詩尤工。

translations.literal: His prose was pure, correct, elegant, and strong; his poetry was especially accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was pure, correct, elegant, and strong; his poetry was especially accomplished.

sentences.zh: 有《經說》二十卷、文集三十卷。

translations.literal: He left twenty fascicles of Expositions on the Classics and thirty fascicles of collected works.
translations.idiomatic: He left twenty fascicles of Expositions on the Classics and thirty fascicles of collected works.

sentences.zh: 二子：逢，仕至司農卿；

translations.literal: He had two sons: Feng, who rose to director of the Directorate of Agriculture;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Feng, who rose to director of the Directorate of Agriculture;

sentences.zh: 逮，亦終敷文閣待制。

translations.literal: and Dai, who also ended as Hanlin academician of the Fuwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: and Dai, who also ended as Hanlin academician of the Fuwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 而逢最以學稱。

translations.literal: Feng was most renowned for his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was most renowned for his learning.

sentences.zh: 兄 開

translations.literal: Elder brother Kai
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Kai

sentences.zh: 開，字天遊。

translations.literal: Kai, courtesy name Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Kai, styled Tianyou.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善屬文。

translations.literal: As a youth he loved learning and was skilled at composition.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved learning and was skilled at composition.

sentences.zh: 崇寧間登進士第，調真州司戶，累遷國子司業，擢起居舍人，權中書舍人。

translations.literal: During the Chongning era he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as revenue recorder of Zhenzhou, was successively promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education, elevated to diarist-attendant, and made acting Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongning era he passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as revenue recorder of Zhenzhou, was successively promoted to vice director of the Directorate of Education, elevated to diarist-attendant, and made acting Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 掖垣草制，多所論駁，忤時相意，左遷太常少卿，責監大寧監鹽井，匹馬之官，不以自卑。

translations.literal: Drafting edicts in the secretariat, he often argued and rebutted, offending the chief minister's intent. He was demoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and ordered to supervise salt wells at the Daning Directorate. He went to his post alone on horseback and did not consider himself debased.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting edicts in the secretariat, he often argued and rebutted, offending the chief minister. He was demoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and ordered to supervise salt wells at the Daning Directorate. He went to his post alone on horseback and did not consider himself debased.

sentences.zh: 召還，時相復用事，監杭州市易務。

translations.literal: Recalled, when the chief minister again held power he supervised the Hangzhou Market Exchange Office.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, when the chief minister again held power he supervised the Hangzhou Market Exchange Office.

sentences.zh: 除直秘閣，知和州，徙知恩州。

translations.literal: He was granted direct access to the Secretariat and appointed prefect of Hezhou, then transferred as prefect of Enzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted direct access to the Secretariat and appointed prefect of Hezhou, then transferred as prefect of Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 請祠，得鴻慶宮，判南京國子監。

translations.literal: He requested a temple post and received the Hongqing Abbey, serving as administrator of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a temple post and received the Hongqing Abbey, serving as administrator of the Nanjing Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 復為中書舍人，罷。

translations.literal: He again became Secretariat drafter and was then dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He again became Secretariat drafter and was then dismissed.

sentences.zh: 提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Abbey.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，除顯謨閣待制、提舉萬壽觀、知潁昌府，兼京西安撫使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne, Kai was appointed Hanlin academician of the Xianmo Pavilion, superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey, prefect of Yingchang, and concurrent pacification commissioner of Jing West.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Qinzong ascended the throne, Kai was appointed Hanlin academician of the Xianmo Pavilion, superintendent of the Wanshou Abbey, prefect of Yingchang, and concurrent pacification commissioner of Jing West.

sentences.zh: 奪職，奉祠。

translations.literal: His post was revoked and he received a temple stipend.
translations.idiomatic: His post was revoked and he received a temple stipend.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，復職，知潭州、湖南安撫使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan his post was restored and he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou and pacification commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyan his post was restored and he was appointed prefect of Tanzhou and pacification commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 逾年求去，復得鴻慶宮，起知平江府、廣東經略安撫使。

translations.literal: After more than a year he requested leave and again received the Hongqing Abbey. He was recalled as prefect of Pingjiang and military commissioner and pacification commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he requested leave and again received the Hongqing Abbey. He was recalled as prefect of Pingjiang and military commissioner and pacification commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 奉詔駐潮陽招捕處寇，訖事，乃之鎮。

translations.literal: By imperial order he stationed at Chaoyang to recruit and suppress bandits. When the task was finished he went to his command.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he stationed at Chaoyang to recruit and suppress bandits. When the task was finished he went to his command.

sentences.zh: 居二年，盡平群盜。

translations.literal: After two years he had completely pacified all the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he had completely pacified all the bandits.

sentences.zh: 提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: He was made superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He was made superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 復以中書舍人召，首論：「自古興衰撥亂之主，必有一定之論，然後能成功。

translations.literal: Again summoned as Secretariat drafter, he first argued: "From antiquity, rulers who rose or fell and quelled disorder always had a fixed plan before they could succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Again summoned as Secretariat drafter, he first argued: "From antiquity, rulers who rose or fell and quelled disorder always had a fixed plan before they could succeed."

sentences.zh: 願講明大計，使議論一定，斷而必行，則功烈可與周宣侔矣。

translations.literal: I hope the great plan will be clarified so that debate is settled, decisions are made and carried out, and then achievements can match those of King Xuan of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: I hope the great plan will be clarified so debate is settled, decisions are made and carried out, and achievements can match those of King Xuan of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」又論：「車駕撫巡東南，重兵所聚，限以大江，敵未易遽犯，其所窺伺者全蜀也。

translations.literal: He also argued: "The imperial carriage pacifies and tours the southeast where heavy forces gather, bounded by the great river—the enemy cannot easily attack suddenly. What they watch for is all of Shu."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued: "The imperial carriage pacifies the southeast where heavy forces gather, bounded by the great river—the enemy cannot easily attack suddenly. What they watch for is all of Shu."

sentences.zh: 一失其防，陛下不得高枕而臥矣。

translations.literal: Once its defense is lost, Your Majesty will not be able to sleep peacefully.
translations.idiomatic: Once its defense is lost, Your Majesty will not be able to sleep peacefully.

sentences.zh: 願擇重臣與吳玠協力固護全蜀。

translations.literal: I hope a weighty minister will be chosen to work with Wu Jie to firmly protect all of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: I hope a senior minister will be chosen to work with Wu Jie to firmly protect all of Shu.

sentences.zh: 」屢請去，進寶文閣待制，知鎮江府兼沿江安撫使。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested leave and was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Baowen Pavilion, prefect of Zhenjiang, and concurrent pacification commissioner along the river.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly requested leave and was promoted to Hanlin academician of the Baowen Pavilion, prefect of Zhenjiang, and concurrent pacification commissioner along the river.

sentences.zh: 召為刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 言：「太祖懲五季尾大不掉之患，畿甸屯營，倍于天下，周廬宿衛，領以三衙。

translations.literal: He said: "Taizu remedied the affliction of the Five Dynasties when regional power grew too great to control. Garrison camps in the capital region were double those elsewhere, and palace guards were led by the Three Bureaus."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Taizu remedied the affliction of the Five Dynasties when regional power grew too great to control. Garrison camps in the capital region were double those elsewhere, and palace guards were led by the Three Bureaus."

sentences.zh: 今禁旅單弱，願參舊制增補之。

translations.literal: Today the palace guard is thin and weak. I hope the old system will be consulted to strengthen it.
translations.idiomatic: Today the palace guard is thin and weak. I hope the old system will be consulted to strengthen it.

sentences.zh: 」帝悉嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor fully praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fully praised and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎兼直學士院。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of rites, concurrently serving in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of rites, concurrently serving in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 時秦檜專主和議，開當草國書，辨視體制非是，論之，不聽，遂請罷，改兼侍讀。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Hui monopolized advocacy of peace. When Kai was to draft the state letter, he examined the format and found it incorrect. He argued against it but was not heeded, so he requested dismissal and was changed to concurrent reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qin Hui monopolized advocacy of peace. When Kai was to draft the state letter, he found the format incorrect. He argued against it but was not heeded, so he requested dismissal and was changed to concurrent reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 檜嘗招開慰以溫言，且曰：「主上虛執政以待。

translations.literal: Hui once summoned Kai and comforted him with kind words, saying: "The sovereign has left the executive post vacant awaiting you."
translations.idiomatic: Hui once summoned Kai and comforted him with kind words, saying: "The sovereign has left the executive post vacant awaiting you."

sentences.zh: 」開曰：「儒者所爭在義，苟為非義，高爵厚祿弗顧也。

translations.literal: Kai said: "What Confucians contend over is righteousness. If something is unrighteous, high rank and thick salary are not considered."
translations.idiomatic: Kai said: "What Confucians contend over is righteousness. If something is unrighteous, high rank and thick salary are not considered."

sentences.zh: 願聞所以事敵之禮。

translations.literal: I wish to hear what rites are used in dealing with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to hear what rites are used in dealing with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」檜曰：「若高麗之於本朝耳。

translations.literal: Hui said: "Like Goryeo toward our dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said: "Like Goryeo toward our dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」開曰：「主上以聖德登大位，臣民之所推戴，列聖之所聽聞，公當強兵富國，尊主庇民，奈可自卑辱至此，非開所敢聞也。

translations.literal: Kai said: "The sovereign ascended the great throne through sacred virtue, acclaimed by ministers and people and heard of by successive sages. You ought to strengthen the army and enrich the state, honor the ruler and protect the people—how can we humiliate ourselves to this extent? This is not something Kai dares to hear."
translations.idiomatic: Kai said: "The sovereign ascended the throne through sacred virtue, acclaimed by ministers and people and heard of by successive sages. You ought to strengthen the army and enrich the state, honor the ruler and protect the people—how can we humiliate ourselves to this extent? This is not something I dare to hear."

sentences.zh: 」又引古誼以折之。

translations.literal: He also cited ancient principles to refute him.
translations.idiomatic: He also cited ancient principles to refute him.

sentences.zh: 檜大怒曰：「侍郎知故事，檜獨不知耶？

translations.literal: Hui grew greatly angry and said: "The vice minister knows precedent—does Hui alone not know it?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui grew greatly angry and said: "The vice minister knows precedent—do I alone not know it?"

sentences.zh: 」他日，開又至政事堂，問計果安出，檜曰：「聖意已定，尚何言！

translations.literal: Another day Kai again came to the chief council hall and asked where the plan truly came from. Hui said: "The sacred intent is already fixed—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: Another day Kai again came to the chief council hall and asked where the plan truly came from. Hui said: "The sacred intent is already fixed—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 公自取大名而去，如檜，第欲濟國事耳。

translations.literal: You take a great reputation and leave. As for Hui, he only wishes to aid the affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: You take a great reputation and leave. As for me, I only wish to aid the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 」然猶以梓宮未還，母后、欽宗未復，詔侍從、臺諫集議以聞。

translations.literal: Yet because the late emperor's coffin had not returned and the empress dowager and Emperor Qinzong had not been restored, an edict ordered attendants and censorial remonstrators to gather for discussion and report.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because the late emperor's coffin had not returned and the empress dowager and Emperor Qinzong had not been restored, an edict ordered attendants and censorial officials to gather for discussion and report.

sentences.zh: 開上疏略曰：「但當修德立政，嚴於為備，以我之仁敵彼之不仁，以我之義敵彼之不義，以我之戒懼敵彼之驕泰，真積力久，如元氣固而病自消，大陽升而陰自散，不待屈己，陛下之志成矣。

translations.literal: Kai submitted a memorial stating in part: "We need only cultivate virtue and establish governance, be strict in preparation, oppose their lack of benevolence with our benevolence, their lack of righteousness with our righteousness, their arrogance and ease with our caution and fear. Truly accumulate strength over time—like vital energy firming so illness dispels itself, the great yang rising so yin scatters of itself—without bowing, Your Majesty's intent will be fulfilled."
translations.idiomatic: Kai submitted a memorial stating in part: "We need only cultivate virtue and establish governance, be strict in preparation, oppose their lack of benevolence with our benevolence, their lack of righteousness with our righteousness, their arrogance with our caution. Truly accumulate strength over time—like vital energy firming so illness dispels itself, the great yang rising so yin scatters—without bowing, Your Majesty's intent will be fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 不然，恐非在天之靈與太后、淵聖所望于陛下者也。

translations.literal: Otherwise I fear this is not what the spirits in Heaven and the empress dowager and Emperor Qinzong hope for from Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I fear this is not what the spirits in Heaven and the empress dowager and Emperor Qinzong hope for from Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」檜曰：「此事大係安危。

translations.literal: Hui said: "This matter greatly concerns safety and danger."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said: "This matter greatly concerns safety and danger."

sentences.zh: 」開曰：「今日不當說安危，只當論存亡。

translations.literal: Kai said: "Today we should not speak of safety and danger—we should speak only of survival and extinction."
translations.idiomatic: Kai said: "Today we should not speak of safety and danger—we should speak only of survival and extinction."

sentences.zh: 」檜矍然。

translations.literal: Hui started in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Hui started in alarm.

sentences.zh: 會樞密編修胡銓上封事，痛詆檜，極稱開，由是罷，以寶文閣待制知婺州。

translations.literal: When Bureau of Military Affairs compiler Hu Quan submitted a sealed memorial fiercely denouncing Hui and greatly praising Kai, Kai was dismissed on this account and made Hanlin academician of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Bureau of Military Affairs compiler Hu Quan submitted a sealed memorial fiercely denouncing Hui and greatly praising Kai, Kai was dismissed and made Hanlin academician of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 開言：「議論妄發，實緣國事。

translations.literal: Kai said: "Reckless speech in debate truly stems from affairs of state."
translations.idiomatic: Kai said: "Reckless speech in debate truly stems from affairs of state."

sentences.zh: 」力請歸。

translations.literal: He forcefully requested to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He forcefully requested to return home.

sentences.zh: 檜議奪職，同列以為不可，提舉太平觀、知徽州。

translations.literal: Hui proposed stripping his post, but colleagues held this unacceptable. Kai was made superintendent of the Taiping Abbey and prefect of Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hui proposed stripping his post, but colleagues held this unacceptable. Kai was made superintendent of the Taiping Abbey and prefect of Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 以病免，居閑十餘年。

translations.literal: Excused on grounds of illness, he lived in retirement for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Excused on grounds of illness, he lived in retirement for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 黃達如請籍和議同異為士大夫升黜，即擢達如監察御史，首劾開，褫職。

translations.literal: Huang Daru requested that agreement or disagreement with the peace talks be registered for the promotion and dismissal of scholar-officials. Daru was immediately promoted to investigating censor and first impeached Kai, stripping his post.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Daru requested that agreement or disagreement with peace talks be registered for the promotion and dismissal of scholar-officials. Daru was immediately promoted to investigating censor and first impeached Kai, stripping his post.

sentences.zh: 引年請還政，僅復秘閣修撰，卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: Citing his age he requested return of office and was restored only as Hanlin academician compiler. He died at the age of seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his age he requested return of office and was restored only as Hanlin academician compiler. He died at seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 檜死，始復待制，盡還致仕遺表恩數。

translations.literal: When Hui died, Kai's Hanlin academician standing was restored and all the favors from his retirement memorial were fully returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui died, Kai's Hanlin academician standing was restored and all the favors from his retirement memorial were fully returned.

sentences.zh: 開孝友厚族，信于朋友。

translations.literal: Kai was filial and friendly, generous to his clan, and trusted among friends.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was filial and friendly, generous to his clan, and trusted among friends.

sentences.zh: 其守歷陽也，從遊酢學，日讀《論語》，求諸言而不得，則反求諸心，每有會意，欣然忘食。

translations.literal: When he governed Liyang he studied under You Zuo, reading the Analects daily. Seeking it in words and not finding it, he turned back to seek it in the heart. Whenever he grasped the meaning he forgot eating in delight.
translations.idiomatic: When he governed Liyang he studied under You Zuo, reading the Analects daily. Seeking it in words and not finding it, he turned back to seek it in the heart. Whenever he grasped the meaning he forgot eating in delight.

sentences.zh: 其留南京，劉安世一見如舊，定交終身。

translations.literal: When he stayed in Nanjing, Liu Anshi at one meeting was like an old friend, and they formed a bond for life.
translations.idiomatic: When he stayed in Nanjing, Liu Anshi at one meeting was like an old friend, and they formed a bond for life.

sentences.zh: 故立朝遇事，臨大節而不可奪，師友淵源，固有所自云。

translations.literal: Therefore in court when affairs arose and great integrity was tested he could not be swayed—the deep sources of his teachers and friends indeed had their origin.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in court when great integrity was tested he could not be swayed—the deep sources of his teachers and friends indeed had their origin.

sentences.zh: 勾濤，字景山，成都新繁人。

translations.literal: Gou Tao, courtesy name Jingshan, was a native of Xinfan in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Tao, styled Jingshan, came from Xinfan in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 登崇寧二年進士第，調嘉州法掾、川陝鑄錢司屬官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Chongning and was assigned as legal assistant in Jiazhou and staff officer in the Sichuan-Shaanxi coinage directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Chongning and was assigned as legal assistant in Jiazhou and staff officer in the Sichuan-Shaanxi coinage directorate.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，通判黔州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan he was vice prefect of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyan he was vice prefect of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 田祐恭兵道境上，濤白守，燕勞之，祐恭感恩厲下，郡得以無犯。

translations.literal: Tian Yougong's troops passed through the border. Tao informed the prefect and entertained and comforted Yougong. Yougong was grateful and disciplined his men, so the prefecture was not violated.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yougong's troops passed through the border. Tao informed the prefect and entertained Yougong. Yougong was grateful and disciplined his men, so the prefecture was not violated.

sentences.zh: 湖湘賊王辟破秭歸，桑仲、郭守忠攻茶務箭窠砦，將犯夔門。

translations.literal: Bandits in Hunan and Hubei—Wang Pi broke Zigui; Sang Zhong and Guo Shouzhong attacked the tea office arrow-nest fort—were about to invade Kuimen.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Hunan and Hubei—Wang Pi broke Zigui; Sang Zhong and Guo Shouzhong attacked the tea office fort—were about to invade Kuimen.

sentences.zh: 夔兵素單弱，宣司檄祐恭捍禦，濤帥黔兵佐之，賊潰去。

translations.literal: Kuai forces had always been thin and weak. The pacification commission ordered Yougong to defend. Tao led Qian troops to assist and the bandits fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Kuai forces had always been thin and weak. The pacification commission ordered Yougong to defend. Tao led Qian troops to assist and the bandits fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 宣撫張浚奏濤知巴州，不赴。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun memorialized to appoint Tao prefect of Bazhou, but he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun memorialized to appoint Tao prefect of Bazhou, but he did not go.

sentences.zh: 翰林侍讀學士范沖薦，召見，論五事，除兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Hanlin reader-in-waiting Fan Chong recommended him. Summoned for audience, he discussed five matters and was appointed director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin reader-in-waiting Fan Chong recommended him. Summoned for audience, he discussed five matters and was appointed director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷右司郎官兼校正。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to director in the Right Bureau, concurrently serving as collator.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to director in the Right Bureau, concurrently serving as collator.

sentences.zh: 日食，上言。

translations.literal: At a solar eclipse he submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At a solar eclipse he submitted a memorial.

sentences.zh: 八月，遷起居舍人，以足疾，命閣門賜墩待班。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was transferred to diarist-attendant. Because of a foot ailment, the Gate Office was ordered to grant him a cushion for waiting in court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was transferred to diarist-attendant. Because of a foot ailment, the Gate Office was ordered to grant him a cushion for waiting in court.

sentences.zh: 九月，兼權中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was concurrently appointed acting Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was concurrently appointed acting Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 時沿邊久宿兵，江、浙罷於饋餉，荊、襄、淮、楚多曠土，濤因進羊祜屯田故事，事下諸大將，於是邊方議行屯田。

translations.literal: At that time troops had long been stationed on the frontier; Jiang and Zhe were exhausted by supply transport; Jing, Xiang, Huai, and Chu had much idle land. Tao therefore presented the precedent of Yang Hu's frontier farming. The matter was sent down to the great generals, and the frontier then debated implementing military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Troops had long been stationed on the frontier; Jiang and Zhe were exhausted by supply; Jing, Xiang, Huai, and Chu had much idle land. Tao presented Yang Hu's frontier-farming precedent, the matter went to the great generals, and the frontier then debated military colonies.

sentences.zh: 淮西都統制劉光世乞罷，丞相張浚欲以呂祉代之，濤謂：「祉疏庸淺謀，必敗事，莫若就擇將士素所推服者用之，否則劉錡可。

translations.literal: Huai West chief commander Liu Guangshi asked to be relieved. Chief Minister Zhang Jun wished to replace him with Lü Zhi. Tao said: "Zhi is shallow in counsel and mediocre in planning—he will surely fail. Better to choose from among generals and soldiers already trusted and respected; otherwise Liu Qi would do."
translations.idiomatic: Huai West chief commander Liu Guangshi asked to be relieved. Chief Minister Zhang Jun wished to replace him with Lü Zhi. Tao said: "Zhi is shallow and mediocre—he will surely fail. Better to choose a general already trusted; otherwise Liu Qi would do."

sentences.zh: 」浚不納，祉至，果以輕易失士心，未幾，酈瓊叛，祉死於亂。

translations.literal: Jun did not accept this. When Zhi arrived he indeed lost the soldiers' hearts through casual conduct. Before long Li Qiong rebelled and Zhi died in the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Jun refused. When Zhi arrived he lost the soldiers' hearts through casual conduct. Before long Li Qiong rebelled and Zhi died in the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 浚聞之，夜半召濤愧謝。

translations.literal: When Jun heard of it he summoned Tao at midnight and apologized in shame.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun heard he summoned Tao at midnight and apologized in shame.

sentences.zh: 時帝駐蹕建康，欲亟還臨安。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was encamped at Jiankang and wished to hurry back to Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was encamped at Jiankang and wished to hurry back to Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 濤入見曰：「今江、淮列戍十餘萬，苟付託得人，可無憂顧。

translations.literal: Tao entered audience and said: "Today more than a hundred thousand troops stand guard along the Jiang and Huai. If entrusted to the right men, there need be no worry."
translations.idiomatic: Tao entered audience and said: "More than a hundred thousand troops stand guard along the Jiang and Huai. Entrusted to the right men, there need be no worry."

sentences.zh: 適此危疑，詎宜輕退，以啟敵心。

translations.literal: At this moment of crisis and doubt, how can we lightly withdraw and stir the enemy's heart?
translations.idiomatic: At this moment of crisis, how can we lightly withdraw and stir the enemy's heart?

sentences.zh: 」因薦劉錡。

translations.literal: He thereupon recommended Liu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon recommended Liu Qi.

sentences.zh: 帝即命以其眾鎮合肥。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered Liu Qi's forces to garrison Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered Liu Qi's forces to garrison Hefei.

sentences.zh: 川、陝宣撫使吳玠言都轉運使李迨朘刻賞格，迨亦奏玠苛費，帝以問濤。

translations.literal: Sichuan-Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner Wu Jie reported that transport commissioner Li Yi was harsh in reward regulations; Yi also memorialized that Jie was wasteful. The emperor asked Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan-Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner Wu Jie reported that transport commissioner Li Yi was harsh in reward regulations; Yi also memorialized that Jie was wasteful. The emperor asked Tao.

sentences.zh: 濤曰：「玠忠在西蜀，縱費，寧可核？

translations.literal: Tao said: "Jie is loyal in western Shu. Even if he spends lavishly, how can we audit him?
translations.idiomatic: Tao said: "Jie is loyal in western Shu. Even if he spends lavishly, how can we audit him?

sentences.zh: 第移迨他路可爾。

translations.literal: Simply transfer Yi to another circuit."
translations.idiomatic: Simply transfer Yi to another circuit."

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 會金人廢劉豫，金、房鎮撫使郭浩遣其弟沔奏事。

translations.literal: When the Jin abolished Liu Yu, Jin-Fang Pacification Commissioner Guo Hao sent his younger brother Bian to report affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin abolished Liu Yu, Jin-Fang Pacification Commissioner Guo Hao sent his younger brother Bian to report affairs.

sentences.zh: 濤察沔警敏可仗，乞詔諭陝右諸叛將乘機南歸，帝命濤草詔，沔持以往，聞者流涕。

translations.literal: Tao saw that Bian was alert and capable and could be relied upon. He asked that an edict instruct the rebel generals of Shaanxi West to seize the moment and return south. The emperor ordered Tao to draft the edict; Bian carried it forth, and those who heard wept.
translations.idiomatic: Tao saw Bian was alert and capable. He asked that an edict instruct Shaanxi rebel generals to seize the moment and return south. The emperor ordered Tao to draft the edict; Bian carried it forth, and those who heard wept.

sentences.zh: 十二月，除中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was appointed Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was appointed Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 八年，除史館修撰。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed compiler of the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed compiler of the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 重修《哲宗實錄》，帝諭之曰：「昭慈聖獻皇后病革，朕流涕問所欲言，後愴然謂朕曰：『吾逮事宣仁聖烈皇后，見其任賢使能，約己便民，憂勤宗社，疏遠外家，古今母后無與為比。

translations.literal: Revising the Veritable Records of Emperor Zhezong, the emperor instructed him: "When Empress Zhaoci Shengxian was critically ill, I wept and asked what she wished to say. The empress said with sorrow: 'I served Empress Xuanren Shengli and saw her employ the worthy, restrain herself to benefit the people, labor for the altars of state, and keep her maternal kin at a distance—no empress in history compares.
translations.idiomatic: Revising the Veritable Records of Emperor Zhezong, the emperor instructed him: "When Empress Zhaoci Shengxian was critically ill, I wept and asked what she wished to say. The empress said with sorrow: 'I served Empress Xuanren Shengli and saw her employ the worthy, restrain herself to benefit the people, labor for the altars of state, and keep her maternal kin at a distance—no empress in history compares.

sentences.zh: 不幸姦邪罔上，史官蔡卞等同惡相濟，造謗史以損聖德，誰不切齒！

translations.literal: Unfortunate wicked men deceived the throne; historiographer Cai Bian and others aided evil together, fabricating slanderous histories to damage sacred virtue—who did not grind their teeth!
translations.idiomatic: Unfortunate wicked men deceived the throne; historiographer Cai Bian and others aided evil, fabricating slanderous histories to damage sacred virtue—who did not grind their teeth!

sentences.zh: 在天之靈亦或介介。

translations.literal: The spirit in Heaven too may be troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit in Heaven too may be troubled.

sentences.zh: 其以筆屬正臣，亟從刪削，以信來世。

translations.literal: Entrust the brush to upright ministers and quickly delete and cut, to be trusted by posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Entrust the brush to upright ministers and quickly delete and cut, to be trusted by posterity.

sentences.zh: 』朕痛念遺訓，未嘗一日輒忘，今以命卿。

translations.literal: I cherish this final instruction and have never forgotten it for a single day. Now I entrust this to you."
translations.idiomatic: I cherish this final instruction and have never forgotten it for a single day. Now I entrust this to you."

sentences.zh: 」濤奏：「數十年來，宰相不學無術，邪正貿亂，所以姦臣子孫得逞其私智，幾亂裕陵成書。

translations.literal: Tao memorialized: "For decades chief ministers have been unlearned and without skill; the wicked and upright have been confused in trade. Therefore the sons and grandsons of treacherous ministers could wield their private schemes and nearly ruined the completed book at Yuling.
translations.idiomatic: Tao memorialized: "For decades chief ministers have been unlearned; the wicked and upright have been confused. Therefore the sons of treacherous ministers nearly ruined the completed book at Yuling.

sentences.zh: 非賴陛下聖明，則任申必先有過嶺之謫，臣亦恐復蹈媒蘖之禍。

translations.literal: Had it not been for Your Majesty's sagacity, Ren Shen would first have suffered exile beyond the Ling range, and your servant too would have feared falling again into the trap of slander."
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been for Your Majesty's sagacity, Ren Shen would first have been exiled beyond the Ling range, and I too would have feared falling into slander again."

sentences.zh: 」帝慰勉之。

translations.literal: The emperor comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 六月，《實錄》成，進一秩，就館賜宴。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Veritable Records were completed. He was promoted one rank and granted a banquet at the institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Veritable Records were completed. He was promoted one rank and granted a banquet at the institute.

sentences.zh: 復修《徽宗實錄》，以中書舍人呂本中為薦，丞相趙鼎諭旨宜婉辭紀載。

translations.literal: He again revised the Veritable Records of Emperor Huizong. On recommendation of Secretariat drafter Lü Benzhong, Chief Minister Zhao Ding instructed that the account should use mild language.
translations.idiomatic: He again revised the Veritable Records of Emperor Huizong. On Lü Benzhong's recommendation, Chief Minister Zhao Ding instructed that the account should use mild language.

sentences.zh: 濤曰：「崇寧、大觀大臣誤國，以稔今禍，藉有隱諱，如天下野史何？」

translations.literal: Tao said: "The chief ministers of Chongning and Daguan misled the state and ripened today's disaster. If we conceal this, what of the unofficial histories under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Tao said: "The chief ministers of Chongning and Daguan misled the state and ripened today's disaster. If we conceal this, what of the unofficial histories under Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 七月，除給事中。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was appointed supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was appointed supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 求去，以徽猷閣待制知池州，改提舉江州太平觀。

translations.literal: He requested leave and was made Hanlin academician of the Huiyou Pavilion and prefect of Chizhou, then changed to superintendent of the Taiping Abbey in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave and was made Hanlin academician of the Huiyou Pavilion and prefect of Chizhou, then changed to superintendent of the Taiping Abbey at Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄除荊湖北路安撫使、知潭州。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed pacification commissioner of Jing-Hu North and prefect of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed pacification commissioner of Jing-Hu North and prefect of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 秦檜嘗令人諭意，欲與共政，濤以書謝之。

translations.literal: Qin Hui once sent someone to convey his intent, wishing to share power with Tao. Tao declined in a letter.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui once sent someone to convey his intent, wishing to share power with Tao. Tao declined in a letter.

sentences.zh: 檜諷言劾之，不報。

translations.literal: Hui hinted that critics should impeach him, but no report was issued.
translations.idiomatic: Hui hinted that critics should impeach him, but no report was issued.

sentences.zh: 濤上書論時事之害政者：「大臣密諭王倫變易地界，一也；

translations.literal: Tao submitted a memorial on current affairs harmful to governance: "First, chief ministers secretly instructed Wang Lun to alter territorial boundaries;
translations.idiomatic: Tao submitted a memorial on current affairs harmful to governance: "First, chief ministers secretly instructed Wang Lun to alter territorial boundaries;

sentences.zh: 蔡攸之妻近居臨平，咫尺行都，略不畏避，二也；

translations.literal: second, Cai You's wife recently lives at Linping, a stone's throw from the mobile court, showing no fear at all;
translations.idiomatic: second, Cai You's wife recently lives at Linping, a stone's throw from the mobile court, showing no fear at all;

sentences.zh: 小大之臣，凡在謫籍，皆已甄敘，惡如京、黼，尚蒙寬宥，今待從之臣，初無大過，理宜牽復，三也；

translations.literal: third, ministers great and small on the demotion register have all been restored, while the wicked like Jing and Fu still receive leniency—yet attendants today with no great fault should logically be restored;
translations.idiomatic: third, ministers on the demotion register have all been restored while the wicked like Jing and Fu still receive leniency—yet attendants with no great fault should be restored;

sentences.zh: 河南故地復歸中國，新附之民，延頸德澤，承流之寄，當加精選，四也；

translations.literal: fourth, the old lands of Henan have returned to China and newly attached people stretch their necks for imperial grace—the posts carrying that grace should be carefully chosen;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, old Henan has returned to China and newly attached people stretch their necks for grace—those carrying it should be carefully chosen;

sentences.zh: 臺諫為耳目之司，今宰相引援，皆同舍之舊，倚為鷹犬，五也。

translations.literal: fifth, the censorate is the court's eyes and ears, yet the chief minister now fills it with old academy classmates used as hunting hawks."
translations.idiomatic: fifth, the censorate is the court's eyes and ears, yet the chief minister fills it with old academy classmates used as hunting hawks."

sentences.zh: 」帝歎其忠直，賜以繒彩、茶藥，且令事有大於此者，悉以聞。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed at his loyalty and forthrightness, granted him silk, tea, and medicine, and ordered that if matters greater than these arose he should report all of them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed at his loyalty, granted him silk, tea, and medicine, and ordered that greater matters be reported.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，提舉太平觀。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was made superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was made superintendent of the Taiping Abbey.

sentences.zh: 十一年，帝謂秦檜曰：「勾濤久閑，性喜泉石，可進職與一山水近郡。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the emperor said to Qin Hui: "Gou Tao has long been idle and loves mountains and streams—promote his rank and give him a prefecture near scenic waters."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the emperor told Qin Hui: "Gou Tao has long been idle and loves mountains and streams—promote him and give him a scenic prefecture."

sentences.zh: 」檜對：「永嘉有天臺、雁蕩之勝。

translations.literal: Hui replied: "Yongjia has the beauties of Tiantai and Yandang."
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied: "Yongjia has Tiantai and Yandang."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「永嘉太遠，其以湖州命之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Yongjia is too far—appoint him to Huzhou."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Yongjia is too far—appoint him to Huzhou."

sentences.zh: 」俄以疾卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: Soon he died of illness at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died of illness at fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 遺表聞，帝震悼，顧近臣曰：「勾濤死矣，惜哉！

translations.literal: When his final memorial was received the emperor was shaken with grief and turned to a close attendant: "Gou Tao is dead—what a pity!
translations.idiomatic: When his final memorial was received the emperor was shaken with grief: "Gou Tao is dead—what a pity!

sentences.zh: 」贈左太中大夫。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Left Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Left Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 濤身長七尺，風貌偉然，頗以忠亮自許。

translations.literal: Tao stood seven feet tall with an imposing bearing and prided himself on loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Tao stood seven feet tall with an imposing bearing and prided himself on loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 國有大議，帝必委心延訪，往復酬詰，率漏下數刻始罷。

translations.literal: When the state faced great deliberations the emperor always entrusted his heart to Tao for extended consultation; back-and-forth questioning often lasted until several marks after the water clock had drained before ending.
translations.idiomatic: When the state faced great deliberations the emperor always consulted Tao at length; questioning often lasted until several marks after the water clock drained.

sentences.zh: 料邊情如在目前，知名之士多所薦進。

translations.literal: He gauged frontier conditions as if they were before his eyes and recommended many renowned men for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He gauged frontier conditions as if before his eyes and recommended many renowned men.

sentences.zh: 有文集十卷，《西掖制書》十卷，奏議十卷。

translations.literal: He left ten fascicles of collected works, ten fascicles of Western Secretariat Drafts, and ten fascicles of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He left ten fascicles of collected works, ten fascicles of Western Secretariat Drafts, and ten fascicles of memorials.

sentences.zh: 李彌遜

translations.literal: Li Mixun
translations.idiomatic: Li Mixun

sentences.zh: 李彌遜，字似之，蘇州吳縣人。

translations.literal: Li Mixun, courtesy name Sizhi, was a native of Wuxian in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mixun, styled Sizhi, came from Wuxian in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，以上舍登大觀三年第，調單州司戶，再調陽穀簿。

translations.literal: In his early twenties, as an upper-hall graduate he passed the examination in the third year of Daguan, was assigned as revenue clerk of Shanzhou, and then transferred as registrar of Yanggu.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties, as an upper-hall graduate he passed in the third year of Daguan, was assigned as revenue clerk of Shanzhou, then transferred as registrar of Yanggu.

sentences.zh: 政和四年，除國朝會要所檢閱文字。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenghe he was appointed collator of texts in the Institute for Compilation of State Documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenghe he was appointed collator of texts in the Institute for Compilation of State Documents.

sentences.zh: 引見，特遷校書郎，充編修六典校閱，累官起成郎。
