translations.literal: Summoned for audience he was specially transferred to collator, appointed compiler-reviewer of the Six Codes, and successively promoted to Gentleman for Attending to Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience he was specially made collator, appointed compiler-reviewer of the Six Codes, and successively promoted to Gentleman for Attending to Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以封事剴切，貶知盧山縣，改奉嵩山祠。

translations.literal: Because his sealed memorial was incisive he was demoted to prefect of Lushan and changed to superintendent of the Songshan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Because his sealed memorial was incisive he was demoted to prefect of Lushan and changed to superintendent of the Songshan Temple.

sentences.zh: 廢斥隱居者八載。

translations.literal: Dismissed and living in seclusion for eight years.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in dismissed seclusion for eight years.

sentences.zh: 宣和末，知冀州。

translations.literal: At the end of Xuanhe he was prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Xuanhe he was prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 金人犯河朔，諸郡皆驚備，彌遜損金帛，致勇士，修城堞，決河護塹，邀擊其遊騎，斬首甚眾。

translations.literal: When the Jin invaded Hebei all prefectures were alarmed and prepared defenses. Mixun reduced gold and silk to recruit brave men, repaired walls and towers, cut the river to protect the moat, intercepted their roaming cavalry, and beheaded many.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin invaded Hebei all prefectures were alarmed. Mixun reduced gold and silk to recruit brave men, repaired walls, cut the river to protect the moat, intercepted roaming cavalry, and beheaded many.

sentences.zh: 兀術北還，戒師毋犯其城。

translations.literal: When Wuzhu returned north he warned his troops not to attack the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzhu returned north he warned his troops not to attack the city.

sentences.zh: 改淮南運副。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice transport commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to vice transport commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 後奉興國宮祠，知饒州，召對，首奏「當堅定規模，排斥姦言」。

translations.literal: Later he received the Xingguo Temple post and was prefect of Raozhou. Summoned for audience he first memorialized that the court must "establish a fixed plan and reject wicked speech."
translations.idiomatic: Later he received the Xingguo Temple post and was prefect of Raozhou. Summoned to audience he first memorialized that the court must establish a fixed plan and reject wicked speech.

sentences.zh: 又謂：「朝廷一日無事，幸一日之安，一月無事，幸一月之安，欲求終歲之安，已不可得，況能定天下大計乎？

translations.literal: He also said: "If the court has no business for one day it congratulates itself on one day's peace; if it has no business for one month it congratulates itself on one month's peace. To seek peace for a whole year is already impossible—how much less can it fix the great plan under Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "One day without trouble means one day's peace; one month without trouble means one month's peace. Peace for a whole year is already impossible—how much less fixing the great plan under Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉其讜直。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his blunt loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised his blunt loyalty.

sentences.zh: 輔臣有不悅者，以直寶文閣知吉州。

translations.literal: Some among the chief ministers were displeased and he was made direct access to the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Some chief ministers were displeased and he was made direct access to the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝曰：「朕欲留卿，大臣欲重試卿民事，行召卿矣。」

translations.literal: At his farewell audience the emperor said: "I wished to keep you, but the chief ministers want to test you further in civil administration—you will soon be recalled."
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor said: "I wished to keep you, but the chief ministers want to test you further in civil administration—you will soon be recalled."

sentences.zh: 七年秋，遷起居郎。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year he was transferred to diarist-attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year he was transferred to diarist-attendant.

sentences.zh: 彌遜自政和末以上封事得貶，垂二十年，及復居是職，直前論事，鯁切如初。

translations.literal: Mixun had been demoted for his sealed memorial at the end of Zhenghe; nearly twenty years passed before he again held this post, yet he spoke forthrightly as sharply as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Mixun had been demoted for his sealed memorial at the end of Zhenghe; nearly twenty years passed before he again held this post, yet he spoke as sharply as at first.

sentences.zh: 冬，試中書舍人，奏六事曰：「固蕃維以禦外侮，嚴禁衛以尊朝廷，練兵以壯國勢，節用以備軍食，收民心以固根本，擇守帥以責實效。

translations.literal: In winter he was examined for Secretariat drafter and memorialized six items: "Strengthen the frontier defenses against external insult, tighten the palace guard to honor the court, drill troops to strengthen national power, economize expenditures to prepare military grain, win the people's hearts to secure the foundation, and choose prefects and commanders to demand real results."
translations.idiomatic: In winter he was examined for Secretariat drafter and memorialized six items: strengthen frontier defenses, tighten the palace guard, drill troops, economize expenditures, win hearts, and choose prefects and commanders for real results.

sentences.zh: 」時駐蹕未定，有旨料舟給卒以濟宮人。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial encampment was not yet fixed; an edict ordered boats and soldiers prepared to ferry palace women.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial encampment was not yet fixed; an edict ordered boats and soldiers prepared to ferry palace women.

sentences.zh: 彌遜繳奏曰：「六飛雷動，百司豫嚴，時方孔艱，宜以宗社為心，不宜於內幸細故，更勤聖慮，事雖至微，懼傷大體。

translations.literal: Mixun returned the memorial stating: "The six dragons move like thunder and the hundred offices stand ready—times are extremely hard. The court should take the altars of state to heart and not trouble the sacred mind over minor matters of inner attendants. Though the affair is tiny, I fear it injures the larger frame."
translations.idiomatic: Mixun returned the memorial: "Times are extremely hard. The court should take the altars of state to heart and not trouble the sacred mind over inner attendants. Though tiny, I fear it injures the larger frame."

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 試戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was examined for vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was examined for vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 秦檜再相，惟彌遜與吏部侍郎晏敦復有憂色。

translations.literal: When Qin Hui became chief minister again, only Mixun and Vice Minister of Personnel Yan Dunfu wore worried expressions.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin Hui became chief minister again, only Mixun and Vice Minister of Personnel Yan Dunfu wore worried expressions.

sentences.zh: 八年，彌遜上疏乞外甚力，詔不允。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Mixun memorialized forcefully requesting an outer appointment; the edict was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Mixun memorialized forcefully requesting an outer appointment; the edict was not granted.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎罷相，檜專國，贊帝決策通和。

translations.literal: When Zhao Ding was dismissed as chief minister, Hui monopolized the state and urged the emperor to decide on peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ding was dismissed, Hui monopolized the state and urged peace.

sentences.zh: 金國遣烏陵思謀等入界，索禮甚悖，軍民皆不平，人言紛紛。

translations.literal: The Jin state sent Wanyan Simo and others across the border, demanding rites in an extremely arrogant manner. Soldiers and civilians were all indignant and public talk was heated.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent Wanyan Simo and others across the border, demanding rites arrogantly. Soldiers and civilians were indignant and talk was heated.

sentences.zh: 檜於御榻前求去，欲要決意屈己從和。

translations.literal: Hui asked to resign before the imperial couch, seeking to force a decision to humble himself and accept peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked to resign before the imperial couch, seeking to force submission to peace.

sentences.zh: 樞密院編修官胡銓上疏乞斬檜，校書郎范如圭以書責檜曲學背師，忘仇辱國，禮部侍郎曾開抗聲引古誼以折檜，相繼貶逐。

translations.literal: Bureau of Military Affairs compiler Hu Quan submitted a memorial asking that Hui be executed; collator Fan Rugui wrote rebuking Hui for perverse learning and betrayal of teachers, forgetting enmity and shaming the state; Vice Minister of Rites Zeng Kai loudly cited ancient principles to refute Hui—they were successively demoted and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Quan asked that Hui be executed; Fan Rugui rebuked Hui for perverse learning and shaming the state; Zeng Kai cited ancient principles to refute him—they were successively demoted.

sentences.zh: 彌遜請對，言金使之請和，欲行君臣之禮，有大不可。

translations.literal: Mixun requested audience and said the Jin envoys, in seeking peace, wished to impose rites between ruler and subject—this was greatly unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Mixun requested audience and said the Jin envoys wished to impose rites between ruler and subject—greatly unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 帝以為然，詔廷臣大議，即日入奏。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and ordered a great court deliberation with memorials submitted that same day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered a great court deliberation with memorials that same day.

sentences.zh: 彌遜手疏力言：「陛下受金人空言，未有一毫之得，乃欲輕祖宗之付託，屈身委命，自同下國而尊奉之，倒持太阿，授人以柄，危國之道，而謂之和可乎？

translations.literal: Mixun submitted a handwritten memorial forcefully stating: "Your Majesty accepts the Jin people's empty words and gains not a single thread—yet you wish to lightly set aside the trust the ancestors placed in you, humble yourself and entrust your fate, treat yourself like a lesser state and honor them, hold the great sword reversed and hand the handle to others. This is the path to endanger the state—can it be called peace?"
translations.idiomatic: Mixun submitted a handwritten memorial: "Your Majesty accepts empty Jin words and gains nothing—yet wishes to set aside ancestral trust, humble yourself like a lesser state, hold the sword reversed and hand others the handle. This endangers the state—can it be called peace?"

sentences.zh: 借使金人姑從吾欲，假以目前之安，異時一有無厭之求，意外之欲，從之則害吾社稷之計，不從則釁端復開，是今日徒有屈身之辱，而後患未已。

translations.literal: Even if the Jin temporarily yielded to our wishes and granted present peace, later when they have insatiable demands or unexpected desires, yielding would harm our plan for the altars of state while refusing would reopen conflict—today we would suffer only the humiliation of bowing while future trouble never ends."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Jin temporarily yielded, later insatiable demands would force a choice: yielding harms our altars while refusing reopens conflict—today's humiliation would never end.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「陛下率國人以事仇，將何以責天下忠臣義士之氣？

translations.literal: He also said: "If Your Majesty leads the people to serve the enemy, how will you charge the loyal and righteous under Heaven with maintaining their spirit?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "If Your Majesty leads the people to serve the enemy, how will you charge loyal men with maintaining their spirit?"

sentences.zh: 」力陳不可者三。

translations.literal: He forcefully set forth three reasons why this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He forcefully set forth three reasons why this could not be done.

sentences.zh: 檜嘗邀彌遜至私第，曰：「政府方虛員，苟和好無異議，當以兩地相浼。

translations.literal: Hui once invited Mixun to his private residence and said: "There are vacant posts in the government. If peace raises no objection, I will recommend you for two offices."
translations.idiomatic: Hui invited Mixun to his residence: "Government posts are vacant. If peace raises no objection, I will recommend you for two offices."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「彌遜受國恩深厚，何敢見利忘義。

translations.literal: He answered: "Mixun has received deep national grace—how dare I see profit and forget righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I have received deep national grace—how dare I see profit and forget righteousness."

sentences.zh: 顧今日之事，國人皆不以為然，獨有一去可報相公。

translations.literal: As for today's affair, the people all disapprove. I have only departure with which to repay the chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: As for today's affair, the people all disapprove. I have only departure with which to repay you."

sentences.zh: 」檜默然。

translations.literal: Hui fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Hui fell silent.

sentences.zh: 次日，彌遜再上疏，言愈切直，又言：「送伴使揣摩迎合，不恤社稷，乞別選忠信之人，協濟國事。

translations.literal: The next day Mixun again submitted a memorial, speaking even more bluntly, and also said: "The escort envoys fawn and comply without caring for the altars of state—I ask that other loyal and trustworthy men be chosen to assist state affairs."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Mixun again submitted a memorial even more bluntly, asking that other loyal men be chosen instead of fawning escort envoys.

sentences.zh: 」檜大怒。

translations.literal: Hui grew greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Hui grew greatly angry.

sentences.zh: 彌遜引疾，帝諭大臣留之。

translations.literal: Mixun pleaded illness; the emperor instructed the chief ministers to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Mixun pleaded illness; the emperor instructed the chief ministers to keep him.

sentences.zh: 時和議已決，附會其說者，至謂「向使明州時，主上雖百拜亦不問」，議論靡然。

translations.literal: Peace was already decided; those who echoed the plan even said, "Even if at Mingzhou the sovereign had bowed a hundred times it would not have mattered"—opinion swirled.
translations.idiomatic: Peace was decided; supporters even said, "Even if at Mingzhou the sovereign had bowed a hundred times it would not have mattered"—opinion swirled.

sentences.zh: 賴彌遜廷爭，檜雖不從，亦憚公論。

translations.literal: Thanks to Mixun's court debate, though Hui did not yield he still feared public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Mixun's court debate, though Hui did not yield he feared public opinion.

sentences.zh: 再與金使者計，議和不受封冊，如宰相就館見金使，受其書納入禁中，多所降殺，惟君臣之禮不得盡爭。

translations.literal: Negotiating again with the Jin envoys, peace was agreed without receiving investiture documents; the chief minister visited the envoys at their lodge, received their letter and brought it into the palace—with many reductions, though the rites between ruler and subject could not be fully contested.
translations.idiomatic: Negotiating again, peace was agreed without investiture documents; the chief minister visited the envoys at their lodge and brought their letter into the palace—with many reductions, though ruler-subject rites could not be fully contested.

sentences.zh: 九年春，再上疏乞歸田，以徽猷閣直學士知端州，改知漳州。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year he again memorialized requesting retirement and was made direct Hanlin academician of the Huiyou Pavilion and prefect of Duanzhou, then changed to prefect of Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year he again requested retirement and was made direct Hanlin academician of the Huiyou Pavilion and prefect of Duanzhou, then changed to Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，歸隱連江西山。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he retired to the mountains of Lianxi in the west.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he retired to the mountains of Lianxi.

sentences.zh: 是歲，兀術分四道入侵，明年，又侵淮西，取壽春，竟如彌遜言。

translations.literal: That year Wuzhu invaded in four columns; the next year he again invaded Huai West and took Shouchun—exactly as Mixun had said.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wuzhu invaded in four columns; the next year he invaded Huai West and took Shouchun—exactly as Mixun had said.

sentences.zh: 十二年，檜乘金兵既敗，收諸路兵，復通和好，追仇向者盡言之臣，嗾言者論彌遜與趙鼎、王庶、曾開四人同沮和議。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, after the Jin army was defeated Hui recalled troops from all circuits and restored peace, pursuing vengeance against those who had spoken out. Instigators memorialized that Mixun, together with Zhao Ding, Wang Shu, and Zeng Kai, had jointly obstructed the peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, after the Jin army was defeated Hui restored peace and pursued those who had spoken out. Instigators memorialized that Mixun, Zhao Ding, Wang Shu, and Zeng Kai had jointly obstructed peace.

sentences.zh: 於是彌遜落職，十餘年間不通時相書，不請磨勘，不乞任子，不序封爵，以終其身，常憂國，無怨懟意。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mixun was dismissed from office. For more than ten years he exchanged no letters with the chief ministers, did not request merit review, did not petition for appointment of his sons, and did not seek enfeoffment of titles, living out his days thus. He constantly grieved for the state yet bore no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Mixun lost his post and, for more than a decade, wrote no letters to the chief ministers, sought no merit review, no appointments for his sons, and no ennoblement—living quietly to the end. He still grieved for the realm and never nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-third year.

sentences.zh: 朝廷思其忠節，詔復敷文閣待制。

translations.literal: The court, mindful of his loyalty and integrity, issued an edict restoring him as Hanlin Attendant Drafting Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering his loyalty, the court restored his title of Hanlin Attendant Drafting Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 有奏議三卷，外制二卷，《議古》三卷，詩十卷。

translations.literal: He left three fascicles of memorials, two fascicles of external edicts, three fascicles of "Discourse on Antiquity," and ten fascicles of poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included three fascicles of memorials, two of external edicts, three of Discourse on Antiquity, and ten of poetry.

sentences.zh: 弟彌大。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Mida.
translations.idiomatic: He had a younger brother, Mida.

sentences.zh: 弟 彌大

translations.literal: Younger brother: Mida
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Mida

sentences.zh: 彌大，字似矩，登崇寧三年進士第。

translations.literal: Mida, courtesy name Simu, passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Chongning.
translations.idiomatic: Mida, styled Simu, earned his jinshi degree in Chongning 3.

sentences.zh: 以大臣薦召對，除校書郎，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: On recommendation of a senior minister he was summoned for audience and appointed Proofreader; he was later promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by a grand minister, he was called to audience, made Proofreader, and later promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 假太常少卿充契丹賀正旦使。

translations.literal: He served as acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices on a mission to congratulate the Khitan on the New Year.
translations.idiomatic: As acting Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices he went as envoy to offer New Year congratulations to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 時傳聞燕民欲歸漢，徽宗遣彌大覘之。

translations.literal: Rumors then circulated that the people of Yan wished to return to the Song, and Emperor Huizong sent Mida to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that the people of Yan wanted to rejoin the Song, Huizong dispatched Mida to reconnoiter.

sentences.zh: 使還，奏所聞有二：「或謂彼主淫刑滅親，種類畔離，女真侵迫，國勢危殆為可取；

translations.literal: On his return he memorialized what he had heard in two parts: "Some say their ruler inflicts cruel punishments and destroys his kin, his people are divided and estranged, the Jurchens press upon them, and the state is perilously near collapse—therefore it may be taken;
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he reported two views: "Some hold that their ruler inflicts cruel punishments and alienates his kin, the tribes are split, Jurchen pressure is mounting, and the realm is near collapse—so it may be seized;

sentences.zh: 或謂下詔罪己，擢用耆舊，招赦盜賊，國尚有人未可取；

translations.literal: others say he has issued an edict blaming himself, promoted the aged and experienced, offered amnesty to bandits, and the state still has men—therefore it may not yet be taken;
translations.idiomatic: others say he has blamed himself in an edict, elevated elders, pardoned rebels, and the country still has loyal men—not yet ripe for conquest;

sentences.zh: 莫若聽其自相攻並。

translations.literal: better to let them attack and consume one another."
translations.idiomatic: best to let them tear one another apart."

sentences.zh: 」 遷起居郎，試中書舍人，同修國史。

translations.literal: " He was promoted to Diarist, tried out as Secretariat Drafting Gentleman, and co-edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: " He was made Diarist, served provisionally as Secretariat Drafting Gentleman, and helped compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 童貫宣撫永興，走馬承受白鍔恃貫不報師期，朝廷止從薄責。

translations.literal: Tong Guan was pacification commissioner in Yongxing; his mounted courier Bai E, relying on Guan, failed to report the campaign schedule, and the court imposed only a light penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan pacified Yongxing, his mounted courier Bai E, shielded by Guan, did not report the army timetable; the court punished him lightly.

sentences.zh: 彌大繳奏，以為邊報不至，非朝廷福。

translations.literal: Mida submitted a sealed memorial arguing that when frontier reports failed to arrive, it was no blessing for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Mida protested in a sealed memorial that missing frontier reports boded ill for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 鍔坐除名，彌大亦出知光州。

translations.literal: Bai E was stripped of rank; Mida was also sent out as prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bai E was dismissed from office, and Mida too was posted out as prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 移知鄂州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later transferred to Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 召為給事中兼校正御前文籍詳定官，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Supervising Censor and concurrently Corrector of the Imperial Archives, and appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Supervising Censor and archive corrector, he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 金人大舉入侵，李綱定城守之策，命彌大為參議，與綱不合，罷。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded on a great scale, Li Gang fixed on a strategy of defending the capital and appointed Mida as deliberation officer; they did not agree and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: During the great Jurchen invasion Li Gang chose to hold the capital and made Mida a deliberation officer; they clashed and Mida was removed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷許割三鎮畀金人，既而遣种師道、師中援河北，姚古援河東，彌大上疏乞起河東西境麟、府諸郡及陝西兵以濟古之師，起河東路及京東近郡兵以濟師道、師中之師，為腹背攻劫之圖。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had agreed to cede the three prefectures to the Jurchens, but then sent Zhong Shidao and Shi Zhong to aid Hebei and Yao Gu to aid Hedong. Mida submitted a memorial asking that troops from the Qin and Fu prefectures on the Hedong and Hexi frontiers and from Shaanxi be raised to reinforce Gu, and troops from Hedong and nearby Jingdong prefectures to reinforce Shidao and Shi Zhong, forming a plan to strike from front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: The court had promised the three prefectures to the Jurchens, then sent Zhong Shidao and Shi Zhong to Hebei and Yao Gu to Hedong. Mida urged raising frontier forces from Qin, Fu, and Shaanxi to help Gu, and Hedong and nearby Jingdong troops to help Shidao and Shi Zhong—for a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 遂除彌大河東宣撫副使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mida was appointed deputy pacification commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Mida was then made deputy pacification commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 張師正領勝捷軍敗於河東，潰歸，彌大誅之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shizheng, commanding the Shengjie Army, was defeated in Hedong and fled back in rout; Mida executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shizheng led the Shengjie Army to defeat in Hedong and fled in disorder; Mida had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 復遣餘卒援真定，餘卒叛。

translations.literal: He again sent the remaining troops to aid Zhending, and the survivors mutinied.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the survivors to relieve Zhending, but they rebelled.

sentences.zh: 宣撫罷，命彌大知陝州。

translations.literal: When the pacification commission was abolished, Mida was ordered to govern Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the pacification post was abolished, he was assigned to govern Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 河東破，小將李彥先來謁，言軍事，彌大壯之，留為將，戍崤、澠間以遏敵。

translations.literal: When Hedong fell, the junior officer Li Yan came first to pay his respects and discuss military affairs; Mida was impressed and kept him as a commander, garrisoning the Xiao and Mian region to block the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After Hedong collapsed, the young officer Li Yan came to report on military affairs; Mida admired him, retained him as a commander, and posted him between Xiao and Mian to hold the enemy.

sentences.zh: 詔遣使召援，彌大未敢進。

translations.literal: An edict sent envoys summoning reinforcements, but Mida did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial envoys called for relief troops, yet Mida hesitated to move forward.

sentences.zh: 會永興帥范致虛糺兵勤王，檄彌大充諸道計議。

translations.literal: Then the Yongxing commander Fan Zhixu mustered troops to aid the throne and issued a proclamation appointing Mida coordinator for all routes.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing commander Fan Zhixu rallied troops for the throne and named Mida coordinator of the various routes.

sentences.zh: 行至方城，道阻，乃率眾赴大元帥府。

translations.literal: Reaching Fangcheng he found the road blocked, so he led his men to the grand marshal headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At Fangcheng the road was blocked, so he marched his force to the grand marshal command.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，除知淮寧府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan he was appointed prefect of Huaining.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 1 he became prefect of Huaining.

sentences.zh: 到郡未幾，杜用等夜叛，彌大縋城出，賊散乃還，坐貶秩。

translations.literal: Shortly after reaching the prefecture, Du Yong and others rebelled by night; Mida lowered himself by rope over the wall and fled, returning only after the rebels dispersed; he was demoted in rank for this.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he took office, Du Yong mutinied at night; Mida escaped over the wall by rope and returned once the rebels broke up, but was reduced in rank.

sentences.zh: 尋召為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝如杭州，命權紹興府，試戶部尚書兼侍讀。

translations.literal: When the emperor went to Hangzhou, Mida was ordered to act as prefect of Shaoxing and provisionally serve as Minister of Revenue and Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor moved to Hangzhou, Mida was made acting prefect of Shaoxing and provisional Minister of Revenue and Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩視師，以彌大為參謀官。

translations.literal: Lu Yihao took command in the field and appointed Mida as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yihao inspected the armies and made Mida his staff officer.

sentences.zh: 彌大奏：「王導、謝安為都督，未嘗離朝廷，今邊圉幸無他，頤浩不宜輕動。

translations.literal: Mida memorialized: "Wang Dao and Xie An as grand marshals never left the court; now the frontier is fortunately free of other troubles—Yihao should not move lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Mida wrote: "When Wang Dao and Xie An served as grand marshals they never left the capital; with the border quiet for now, Yihao ought not march lightly."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「已為天子從官，非宰相可辟。

translations.literal: " He also said: "I am already a personal attendant of the Son of Heaven—not someone a chief minister may simply summon."
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "I am already the emperor's personal attendant—not an official a prime minister may simply conscript."

sentences.zh: 乞于諸軍悉置軍正，如漢朝故事，以察官、郎官為之。

translations.literal: He asked that every army be given a military inspector on the Han model, drawn from palace and department officials.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that each army receive a military inspector, as in Han practice, chosen from court and department officials.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲留臣，當別為一司，伺察頤浩過失。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty insists on keeping me, establish a separate office to watch Yihao's faults.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty must keep me, let a separate office monitor Yihao's errors.

sentences.zh: 」忤旨，出知平江府。

translations.literal: " His words offended the throne and he was sent out as prefect of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial angered the throne and he was posted to Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 中丞沈與求劾彌大謀間君臣，妄自尊大，奪職歸。

translations.literal: Censor Shen Yuqiu impeached Mida for scheming between ruler and minister and arrogant self-importance; his office was stripped and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Shen Yuqiu accused Mida of driving a wedge between sovereign and minister and of arrogance; he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 起知靜江府，奏廣西邊防利害。

translations.literal: He was later appointed prefect of Jingjiang and memorialized on the advantages and dangers of the Guangxi frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Later made prefect of Jingjiang, he submitted a memorial on Guangxi frontier strengths and risks.

sentences.zh: 入為工部尚書。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷去。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed again before long.

sentences.zh: 廣西提刑韓璜劾其在靜江日斷強盜死罪，引絞入斬，貶兩秩。

translations.literal: Guangxi intendant Han Huang impeached him for, while at Jingjiang, sentencing a violent robber to death by substituting decapitation for strangulation; he was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi intendant Han Huang charged that at Jingjiang he had upgraded a robber's sentence from strangulation to decapitation; Mida was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 紹興十年卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died in the tenth year of Shaoxing, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shaoxing 10, at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宋既南渡，日以徽宗梓宮及韋后為念。

translations.literal: The commentators say: After the Song crossed south, day by day they kept in mind Emperor Huizong's coffin and Empress Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The historians observe: Once the Song fled south, the court never ceased to think of Huizong's coffin and Empress Wei.

sentences.zh: 秦檜主和，甘心屈己。

translations.literal: Qin Hui advocated peace and willingly humbled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui led the peace faction and willingly abased himself.

sentences.zh: 張燾連章論列，謀深慮遠，其言取必於天，豈忘宗社之仇哉，亦曰相時而動耳！

translations.literal: Zhang Dao submitted memorial after memorial with far-reaching counsel; his words sought certainty from Heaven—had he forgotten the feud against the altars of state? He too said: act according to the times!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dao's repeated memorials were deeply considered; he spoke as if seeking Heaven's verdict—yet had he forgotten the nation's wrong? He too meant to move with the moment!

sentences.zh: 惜其利澤專於蜀也。

translations.literal: It is a pity that his benefits flowed only to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Regrettably, his good deeds benefited Shu alone.

sentences.zh: 黃中不黨不阿，明察料敵，立朝忠實，退不忘君。

translations.literal: Huang Zhong stood neither with factions nor under flattery; he discerned the enemy clearly, served the court faithfully, and in retirement did not forget his sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zhong was independent and unyielding, read the enemy shrewdly, served loyally in office, and in retirement still remembered his ruler.

sentences.zh: 道夫受知張浚，憂國而不為身謀。

translations.literal: Daofu won Zhang Jun's trust and grieved for the state without scheming for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu gained Zhang Jun's confidence and put the nation ahead of personal gain.

sentences.zh: 曾幾積學潔行，風節凜凜，陳嘗膽枕戈之言，以贊親征，亦壯矣哉！

translations.literal: Zeng Ji accumulated learning and pure conduct, his integrity austere; he spoke of tasting gall and sleeping on weapons to support the emperor's personal campaign—how bold!
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Ji's scholarship and rectitude were rigorous; his call to taste gall and sleep on spears in support of the emperor's expedition was truly stirring!

sentences.zh: 勾濤直節正論，不受檜私，潔身歸老。

translations.literal: Gou Tao held to upright principle and honest debate, accepted no favor from Hui, and retired in clean integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Tao spoke with straight principle, took no private favor from Hui, and withdrew to live honorably in old age.

sentences.zh: 彌遜、曾開同沮和議，廢絀以沒，無怨懟心，所謂臨大節而不可奪者歟！

translations.literal: Mixun and Zeng Kai alike blocked the peace talks, were dismissed and demoted until death, yet bore no resentment—are these not men whom great crisis could not sway!
translations.idiomatic: Mixun and Zeng Kai both resisted peace, were cast out and died in obscurity, yet never complained—men whom no crisis could break!
